title: Use-case proposal: payment-gated self-hosted vLLM for agents (HTTP 402 + Nano)
body:
# Use-case / pattern proposal: payment-gated, self-hosted vLLM endpoints for AI agents (HTTP 402 + Nano)

**The use case:** teams self-host vLLM behind its OpenAI-compatible server and want to let *autonomous agents* pay for inference **per token** — without creating accounts, issuing API keys to every agent, or routing each micro-payment through a card processor (which is unusable at sub-cent scale for machines).

vLLM's OpenAI-compatible server already returns per-request usage (`prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens`), so the meter exists. This is a proposal about the **thin, out-of-process layer in front of it** — not a change to vLLM internals.

**The pattern (already proven elsewhere, mentioned here for reference):** the open x402 protocol turns HTTP into a native payment channel: server returns `402 Payment Required` with payment terms, the paying client settles on-chain and retries with an `X-PAYMENT` header. A related 402 pay-per-token proxy example was proposed for the LiteLLM gateway (BerriAI/litellm#38688), and Nano (XNO) gives the same pattern **zero fees and sub-second finality** — so a self-hosted vLLM endpoint can charge, say, 0.000001 XNO per call without a fee floor eating the payment. Nano building blocks that make this a thin adapter, not a from-scratch rail:
- `@x402nano/exact` (Client / Resource Server / Facilitator) — https://github.com/x402nano/exact
- `x402nano/facilitator` and a publicly runnable `nanoroute` facilitator with a public node — https://github.com/robgilmore26/nanoroute

Because Eth-L2/USDC x402 facilitators and 402 pay-per-token middleware already exist, this is not asking vLLM to build a payments feature — it is demonstrating that a **self-hosted vLLM endpoint can be agent-payable today** behind a ~100-line gateway, and asking whether the vLLM project would like such an `examples/` reference or a documented how-to, reviewed by a human maintainer rather than pushed as an automated change (per vLLM's contribution policy).

**What I'd like from vLLM:** (1) a thumbs-up / feedback on whether a documented "run vLLM behind a 402 pay-per-token gateway" example would be a welcome addition to the repo or docs, and (2) any maintainer view on the right seam to hang it off (OpenAI-compatible server, the `--api-key` auth path, or a documented reverse-proxy pattern). Happy to keep the middleware fully out-of-band from vLLM core.

If issues are not the right home for this, direct me to where it belongs and I'll take it there.

title: [Bug]: Qwen4Exp PinnedHost PLE prefetch reads n-gram ids from graph-pool memory that later segments reuse
body:
### Your current environment

DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=1, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13, vLLM main (`1ea7c63f4` nightly wheel), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next,
MTP n=3, `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding.start_prefetch`
([ngram_embedding.py#L493-L506](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9f07d023d/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py#L493-L506))
launches the lookup on a side stream and returns; `_finalize_prefetch` joins later. The `gathered_ids` it reads come
from a captured graph segment, so they live in the graph pool. Once `start_prefetch` returns, later segments can reuse
that memory, and at replay the main stream may overwrite the ids while the side stream is still reading them
(`record_stream` does not cover graph-pool memory). The effect is silent: greedy outputs stop being reproducible.

Measured with a backend that runs exactly this flow and differs only in row storage (a pageable file mapping, #58439).
Protocol: 8 greedy prompts, cold vs warm, within one server start.

| lookup | cold == warm | max \|Δlogprob\| |
|---|---|---|
| side stream, ids from the graph pool (this flow) | 2/8 | 1.41 |
| same + #57785 | 1/8 | 1.41 |
| side stream, ids copied to a persistent buffer first | **8/8** | 0 |
| current stream | **8/8** | 0 |

Caveat: PinnedHost itself could not run here, because its pinned table does not fit in 128 GB of unified memory.
Pinned reads are faster, so the window should be narrower; not reproduced on PinnedHost itself.

Possible fix: copy `gathered_ids` into a persistent (non-pool) buffer on the current stream before the side-stream
launch (row 3), or look up on the current stream (row 4, which loses the overlap).

*AI assistance: prepared with Claude; measurements run and checked by the submitter.*

title: [Bug]: When using the V4 parser in vLLM to parse outputs from DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the leading extra space in V4.1 DSML tags breaks state machine matching and parameter regex, filters arg deltas, and prevents streaming return of tool call arguments.
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug vLLM does not ship a dedicated parser for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and reuses the existing V4 parser to process model outputs generated by V4.1 Flash. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash introduces an extra leading space inside DSML tags compared to the V4 specification. This difference triggers multiple failures in the legacy V4 parser: 1. The state machine for DSML tag matching fails to recognize tags due to the unexpected leading space. 2. The hardcoded regular expressions used in `_dsml_arg_converter` cannot match the parameter content, as the regex patterns do not account for the leading space. 3. The argument delta filtering logic with `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` buffers all delta content that does not contain the `>` character and suppresses incremental streaming delivery. As a combined result, tool call arguments cannot be streamed back to the caller. The proposed fix is to implement a new V4.1-specific parser inheriting from the V4 parser class: adjust tag definitions and regular expressions to accommodate the leading space, disable the arg delta filtering logic, and register the parser under an independent name. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Roadmap] Rust Frontend Feature Parity
body:
## Motivation

The Rust frontend has landed in the vLLM repository as a drop-in alternative to the Python API server process. It is enabled through `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and uses the existing vLLM engine/core boundary.

The Rust frontend is still experimental and not yet feature-complete relative to the Python frontend. This issue tracks the roadmap for the remaining gaps in feature parity and provides community contributors with a place to find scoped work.

This roadmap prioritizes user value and the Rust frontend's architectural goals over blanket 1:1 parity with the Python frontend. In particular, we may skip:

- Features / endpoints / options that are not commonly used in production
- Options that mainly reflect Python frontend implementation details or Python-side workarounds
- Features whose Python implementation has accumulated enough complexity that redesigning or removing them may be better than porting them directly

**For items marked with 🧭:** Please start with a design discussion before implementation, covering the intended API/architecture, co-design with the engine if needed, and the testing plan.

Related context:

- Original RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40846
- Integration PRs
  * https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40848
  * https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43283

## Current status

- [x] Rust code lives in the main vLLM repository under `rust/`
- [x] `vllm-rs` integrates with `vllm serve` as a Python-supervised frontend subprocess
- [x] Core `/v1/chat/completions` support (streaming & non-streaming)
- [x] Core `/v1/completions` support (streaming & non-streaming)
- [x] Tool calling and reasoning output support for several key model families
- [x] Commonly used OpenAI-compatible sampling options
- [x] Image, audio, and video multimodal chat inputs for registered processor/model specs
- [x] Multi-engine internal load balancing with scheduler-stat-aware routing
- [x] Admin and operational routes: health, load, version, metrics, reset-cache, sleep/wake
- [x] Mock-engine and HTTP integration-test infrastructure for Rust frontend development

## Roadmap

### Distributed serving and large-scale control plane

- [x] External DP load-balancing mode: support the Python-style shape where each API server connects to one DP rank 🧭
- [x] Hybrid DP load-balancing mode: support per-node internal LB plus cross-node external LB 🧭
- [ ] Elastic EP support: implement `/scale_elastic_ep`, `/is_scaling_elastic_ep`, request draining, and scaling-state rejection behavior 🧭
- [ ] Fault tolerance for DP+EP external-LB deployments: `--enable-fault-tolerance`, `/fault_tolerance/apply`, and `/fault_tolerance/status` 🧭
- [x] KV-event publisher discovery: `/kv_event_sources`

### Scale-out and disaggregated serving

### Additional APIs

- [ ] Non-stateful Responses API: start with `POST /v1/responses` without requiring durable response storage 🧭

### Request compatibility and validation

### RL / admin / lifecycle APIs

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.x sparse indexer: the replicated key norm is autotuned per rank, so TP ranks can select different candidates and greedy completions change from launch to launch
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM source commit `385dce36bcee42309924a5ece951a96db3dce7f2`, in image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:b0501f99fec5136f248f78d5850977a2ec32d55cd9a665f4a9ffef24cbdf7fe5`, with local patches unrelated to the indexer's key path. The same code is on `main` at `36f94d5fe8a3` (2026-09-24).
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04.3 (aarch64).
- 2 × NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark class), TP=2 over RoCE, driver 580.173.02.
- Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (and a requantized derivative), MTP depth 3, `--enforce-eager`, temperature 0.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The kpool sparse indexer in `vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py` is replicated on every TP rank: `wq_b` is a `ReplicatedLinear` and `wk_weights_proj` uses `disable_tp=True`, so each rank computes the same keys and candidate sets from the same inputs. That only works if the ranks compute them **bit-identically**. Nothing enforces this, and one step in the key path does not guarantee it.

The key is normalised by `_fused_indexer_k_norm(kw[:, :head_dim], ...)`, a leaf compiled with `torch.compile(dynamic=True)`. Inductor turns it into a persistent reduction with three candidate configs (`XBLOCK` 1, 8 and 32, `num_warps` 2), and each rank picks one by benchmarking the first time it runs. `XBLOCK=1` computes the row reduction in a different order: on a fixed strided input of 2,048 × 160 → `[:, :128]`, its output differs from `XBLOCK` 8 and 32 in 2 of 2,048 rows (8 and 32 agree; the same classes on both GPUs). The difference is small, but the indexer then selects the top 512 of 540 pools per row. Where pools are close to a tie, a slightly different key selects a different set on one rank. The two ranks' attention outputs then differ, the all-reduce mixes them, and the greedy completion forks.

What we observed on the two-GPU pair, with everything else fixed (weights verified identical across launches by digest, same image and profile):

| rank 0 config / rank 1 config | Launch state | Ranks' keys differ in | Candidate sets differ in |
|---|---|---|---|
| {8, 32} / {8, 32} | state 1 | 0 of 858 indexer calls | 0 |
| {8, 32} / 1 | state 2 | 10 of 792 (8 of 11 MLA layers, from the first) | 2 (layer 19) |
| 1 / {8, 32} | state 3 | 13 of 836 | 2 (layer 19) |

Each state gives its own bit-reproducible set of completions for our fixed prompts; requests repeat exactly within a launch. So "which completion does this server give at temperature 0" depended on which config each rank's benchmark happened to pick at startup. Across the 16 launches we recorded with per-rank benchmarking, we saw state 1 11 times, state 2 3 times and state 3 twice.

Causality was shown by intervention, not only by correlation: we pinned only this kernel's config before the model loaded. `8 / 1` reproduced state 2, with a request trace identical row for row to an earlier naturally occurring state-2 launch. `8 / 8` restored state 1. Between the two arms, the only hash that changed was rank 1's output of this kernel on a fixed input.

### Why the obvious fix does not work today

`TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC=1` should make Inductor select one reduction config without benchmarking, the same on every rank. With a torch 2.13 bug it does not survive the first compiled frame: Dynamo's global-state restore calls `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(False)`, which also sets `torch._inductor.config.deterministic = False` (reported as pytorch/pytorch#198563). Forcing the entry (`torch._inductor.config._config["deterministic"].env_value_force = True`, set right after the config module is imported) made it work. Both ranks then served the kernel with `XBLOCK=8`, cache state "only 1 config", keys identical on every call, with decode speed within ±3 %. Pointwise leaves still autotune per rank; since each element is computed by the same instructions, their block size should not change the bits (not measured).

### Suggested fixes (for the maintainers to judge)

1. Make the replicated key path deterministic by construction. For example, compute the key norm eagerly in fp32 (it is 128 wide and small), or pin its config, so it does not depend on a per-rank benchmark.
2. Or give each selected row a single owner. The prefill and decode row-sharding PRs (#54394, #58536) compute each row on one rank and all-gather the int32 indices, which removes cross-rank disagreement in the selection. Their motivation is performance, and #58536 applies only to uniform decode batches of 8 or more requests, so small-batch serving keeps the replicated path.
3. In general, any computation that is replicated across TP ranks and feeds a discrete choice (top-k, argmax) needs either bit-identical kernels or a single writer. Inductor leaves in model code autotune per rank and give no such guarantee.

title: Bug: missing colon in logits processor FQCN crashes engine init with unhelpful ValueError
body:
## Bug

In `_load_logitsprocs_by_fqcns()` (`vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/__init__.py`, line 128), the code does:

```python
module_path, qualname = logitproc.split(":")
```

If the user passes a plain dotted path like `"mypackage.mymodule.MyLogitsProcessor"` (missing the required `:`), Python raises:

```
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
```

This error is unhandled and crashes engine initialization. The same crash occurs with two colons (e.g. `"my:package:MyClass"`). Neither case produces a message explaining the expected format.

## Expected format

The docstring says FQCNs must be `<module>:<type>`, e.g. `x.y.z:CustomLogitProc`, but the code does not validate this before unpacking.

## Fix

Replace the bare unpack with a `len(parts) != 2` guard that raises a descriptive `ValueError` naming the expected format.

title: BUG: ValueError (not enough values to unpack) when logits processor FQCN is missing ':' separator
body:
## What breaks

When a user passes a logits processor as a string FQCN (fully-qualified class name) that is missing the required colon separator — for example \`\"mymodule.MyCustomLogitsProcessor\"\` instead of \`\"mymodule:MyCustomLogitsProcessor\"\` — \`_load_logitsprocs_by_fqcns\` in \`vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/__init__.py\` crashes with a confusing Python unpack error rather than a user-friendly message.

## Trigger

Pass any string without \`:\` to \`logits_processors\` in \`LLM\` or via the API, e.g.:

\`\`\`python
llm = LLM(model="...", logits_processors=["mymodule.MyCustomLogitsProcessor"])
\`\`\`

## Traceback

\`\`\`
File "vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/__init__.py", line 128, in _load_logitsprocs_by_fqcns
    module_path, qualname = logitproc.split(":")
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
\`\`\`

## Root cause

Line 128 does \`logitproc.split(":")\` with no guard for the case where the string contains no colon. The docstring documents the required \`<module>:<type>\` syntax but the code performs no validation before the unpack.

## Expected behavior

A clear \`ValueError\` explaining the required format, e.g. \`"Logits processor FQCN 'mymodule.MyCustomLogitsProcessor' is missing the required ':' separator. Expected format: '<module>:<type>'"\`.

title: [Feature]: Add separate_reasoning option for OpenAI chat completion API
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Problem

Currently vLLM OpenAI-compatible chat completion responses expose reasoning separately:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "reasoning": "...",
    "content": "..."
  }
}
```
Some OpenAI-compatible clients, SDKs, and agent frameworks expect all generated text to appear in content only and do not parse the reasoning field.

As a result, users currently need to add custom post-processing logic on the client side to merge reasoning back into content.

## Proposed feature

Add a new optional request parameter:

separate_reasoning: bool = True

Behavior:

separate_reasoning=True (default)
Keep existing behavior
Return reasoning and content separately
```json
{
  "reasoning": "...",
  "content": "..."
}
```
separate_reasoning=False
Merge reasoning into content
Suppress the reasoning field
```json
{
  "content": "<reasoning><content>"
}
```
## Motivation

This improves compatibility with:

Existing OpenAI-compatible APIs
SDKs and client libraries that only consume content
Agent frameworks that do not understand a separate reasoning field
Existing applications migrating to vLLM without additional response transformations

## Why this approach
No breaking changes
Default behavior remains unchanged
Requires minimal changes
Applies consistently to both streaming and non-streaming responses

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

title: CUDA illegal memory access in FP8 MoE moe_permute with cutlass backend at batch size 8192
body:
## Bug Description

vLLM crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` during FP8 MoE inference when the scheduled batch hits exactly 8192 tokens. The crash occurs in the CUTLASS MoE permutation kernel.

## Environment

- vLLM version: 0.17.1 (via `ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-cuda:v0.6.0`)
- GPU: NVIDIA H200 (140GB)
- Model: `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-dynamic` (128 experts, top-2 routing, compressed-tensors FP8)
- TP=1, single GPU
- `max_model_len=2100`, `enable_prefix_caching=True`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-dynamic with vLLM v0.17.1
2. Send ~100 concurrent requests with `prompt_tokens=1000, max_tokens=1`
3. vLLM schedules 9 requests in one batch (8×1001 + 1×184 = 8192 total tokens)
4. Engine crashes on the first model execution step

## Stack Trace

```
File "/opt/vllm-source/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/moe_permute_unpermute.py", line 90, in moe_permute
    a1q_scale = a1q_scale[permuted_idx.clamp(max=n_token * topk - 1) // topk]
                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

Full call chain:
```
core.py:1102 → EngineCore fatal error
  → gpu_worker.py:728 execute_model
    → gpu_model_runner.py:3639 execute_model
      → qwen3_moe.py:783 forward
        → cutlass_moe.py:357 apply (run_cutlass_moe_fp8)
          → moe_permute_unpermute.py:90 moe_permute
            → CUDA illegal memory access
```

## Scheduler State at Crash

From the dump:
```
total_num_scheduled_tokens = 8192
num_running_reqs = 17
num_waiting_reqs = 82
step_counter = 0  (first step after startup)
kv_cache_usage = 0.016
```

9 new requests scheduled, 8 with 1001 tokens each, 1 with 184 tokens. The last request got partial block allocation (`block_ids=([146, 147, 148])` = only 3 blocks vs 16 for the others).

## Analysis

The crash happens at `total_num_scheduled_tokens=8192` which is a CUDA graph capture boundary size (visible in the config: `cudagraph_capture_sizes: [1, 2, 4, 8, ..., 512]` with `max_cudagraph_capture_size: 512` and `compile_ranges_split_points: [8192]`).

The `permuted_idx` tensor in `moe_permute` appears to have out-of-bounds indices when processing FP8 quantized weights with the CUTLASS MoE backend at this specific batch size. The issue is in the FP8 scale indexing: `permuted_idx.clamp(max=n_token * topk - 1) // topk` produces indices that exceed `a1q_scale`'s first dimension.

## Workaround

Setting `--max-num-batched-tokens` to a value other than 8192 (e.g., 4096 or 16384) avoids the crash.

## Expected Behavior

vLLM should handle FP8 MoE models at any batch size without CUDA memory access errors.

title: SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence and spurious trust_remote_code warnings on startup
body:
## Bug Description

Two minor issues on every vLLM startup:

### 1. SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence `\e`

```
/opt/vllm-source/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py:346: SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence '\e'
  "(e.g. 'abcdabcdabcd...' or '\emoji \emoji \emoji ...'). This feature "
/opt/vllm-source/vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py:176: SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence '\e'
  "(e.g. 'abcdabcdabcd...' or '\emoji \emoji \emoji ...'). This feature "
```

The string literal contains `\emoji` which Python interprets as an invalid escape sequence. Should be either a raw string (`r"..."`) or use `\\emoji`.

**Files:**
- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py:346`
- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py:176`

### 2. Spurious `trust_remote_code` warning

```
(APIServer pid=1) The argument `trust_remote_code` is to be used with Auto classes. It has no effect here and is ignored.
(APIServer pid=1) The argument `trust_remote_code` is to be used with Auto classes. It has no effect here and is ignored.
```

This warning is printed twice on every startup when `--trust-remote-code` is passed, even for models that DO use custom code (e.g., Qwen3-MoE). The warning comes from HuggingFace transformers when `trust_remote_code` is passed to a non-Auto class. vLLM should either suppress this warning or not pass the flag to classes that don't need it.

## Environment

- vLLM version: 0.17.1 (via `ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-cuda:v0.6.0`)
- Python 3.12
- Model: RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-dynamic (reproduces with any model)

## Impact

Low severity — these are cosmetic warnings that don't affect functionality. However, they clutter logs and can confuse users running automated log analysis. The SyntaxWarning will become a SyntaxError in a future Python version.

title: [deepseek_v4] DeepSeekV4MTP loader silently skips top-level head.weight + embed.weight → 0% MTP draft acceptance with no error
body:
## Summary

`vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.mtp.DeepSeekV4MTP.load_weights` silently skips top-level `head.weight` and `embed.weight` when the saved artifact stores them at the top level (not as `mtp.0.head.weight` / `mtp.0.emb.tok_emb.weight`). The MTP layer's `shared_head.head` (ParallelLMHead) and `embed_tokens` (VocabParallelEmbedding) stay uninitialized → MTP draft head emits garbage logits → **0% MTP acceptance with no load-time error**. Speculative decoding produces draft tokens that are 100% rejected by the verifier.

## Mechanism

`DeepSeekV4MTP.load_weights` runs this loop:
```python
for name, loaded_weight in weights:
    name = name.replace("mtp.0.", "")  # no-op on top-level keys like "head.weight"
    spec_layer = get_spec_layer_idx(name)
    if spec_layer is None:
        continue  # ← top-level head.weight, embed.weight die here
    ...
```

For a key like `head.weight`:
- `name.replace("mtp.0.", "")` returns `head.weight` unchanged
- `get_spec_layer_idx("head.weight")` returns `None`
- Loop hits `continue` → key never routed to the MTP layer
- MTP layer constructed `shared_head.head` as ParallelLMHead but no weight ever assigned → keeps init random values

## Repro

1. Save a DSv4-Flash artifact via `transformers.save_pretrained` (the canonical path). MTP weights land at upstream naming `mtp.0.*` but `head.weight` + `embed.weight` stay at top level.
2. Serve with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`.
3. Watch `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total / vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total`. Result: drafts produced, accepted = 0.

We hit this exact scenario in [`canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp) iteration 9. Smoke artifact had 797 `mtp.0.*` keys at first and got 0% acceptance silently. Diagnosis trace in [`FINDINGS_FOR_SIBLING.md`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/blob/main/FINDINGS_FOR_SIBLING.md) §C14.

## Workaround (production-validated)

Postprocess injects `mtp.0.head.weight` (FP32 copy of `head.weight`) and `mtp.0.emb.tok_emb.weight` (BF16 copy of `embed.weight`) as full duplicates. Working example: [`scripts/fixup_artifact.py`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/blob/main/scripts/fixup_artifact.py). The sibling artifact `canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP` applies the same pattern (799 mtp.* keys vs our pre-fix 797 — the 2 deltas are these aliases).

After the workaround, MTP acceptance lands at 69.94% over 200 random prompts (raw data in [`benchmarks/phase2/acc_*.json`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/tree/main/benchmarks/phase2)).

## Suggested fix

Option A — `DeepSeekV4MTP.load_weights` should explicitly route top-level `head.weight` to `mtp.{N}.shared_head.head.weight` and top-level `embed.weight` to `mtp.{N}.embed_tokens.weight` (one line added before the `continue`):

```python
for name, loaded_weight in weights:
    # Re-route top-level head/embed to the MTP slot (model-level keys that
    # the MTP draft tower needs but get filtered out by the spec-layer check)
    extra = []
    for layer_off in range(self.config.num_nextn_predict_layers):
        if name == "head.weight":
            extra.append((f"mtp.{layer_off}.shared_head.head.weight", loaded_weight))
        elif name == "embed.weight":
            extra.append((f"mtp.{layer_off}.embed_tokens.weight", loaded_weight))
    if extra:
        # process each routing manually + continue
        for n, w in extra: weight_loader(n, w)
        continue
    # ... existing mtp.0. routing
```

Option B — raise at construction time when `shared_head.head` / `embed_tokens` end up uninitialized. Either is fine; silent 0% acceptance is the worst possible failure mode for spec-decode.

## Severity

Anyone who quantizes DSv4-Flash and ships an artifact via the standard `transformers.save_pretrained` path will hit this silently. The sibling NVFP4 team hit it and worked around it; we hit it independently and worked around it; future MTP-preserving quantizations will hit it too unless this is fixed in the loader.

title: [Feature]: [RFC] Bottleneck-aware expansion for PD disaggregation
body:
This is an RFC-style feature request for discussion.

I have been reading through the recent PD, KV transfer, and offloading work, and it feels like the next missing step is not replacing PD, but making PD deployments more adaptive when one side becomes the dominant bottleneck.

## Summary

This proposal does **not** replace PD disaggregation.

Instead, it builds on the current PD model and asks whether vLLM should identify the dominant bottleneck at runtime and expand the most effective side first.

Concretely, the idea is:

- keep the current PD architecture
- detect whether runtime pressure is mainly on `prefill`, `decode`, or `decode-side KV capacity`
- expand the easiest and most effective side first
- reduce user-facing contention before relying on stronger competition inside a fixed topology

## Motivation

PD already gives an important separation between prefill and decode pools, and KV transfer / request migration / offloading are all moving in the right direction.

But even with PD, deployments still seem mostly statically provisioned. That means it is still easy to end up in situations like:

- `prefill` is saturated while `decode` is relatively idle
- `decode` is saturated while `prefill` is underutilized
- `decode-side KV capacity` becomes the dominant bottleneck even when compute is still available
- remote KV transfer backlog creates hidden stalls between the two pools

So from my perspective, PD solves mixed-pool interference, but not yet dynamic imbalance between the pools.

## Proposal

Introduce a bottleneck-aware expansion layer for PD disaggregation.

A simple first version could classify runtime pressure into three categories:

1. `Prefill-bound`
   Prefill-side compute or memory pressure dominates.

2. `Decode-bound`
   Decode-side token throughput or scheduling pressure dominates.

3. `Decode-KV-bound`
   Decode-side KV holding capacity dominates, even if decode compute is not yet saturated.

Then the runtime (or a future policy layer built on top of it) could choose the most effective expansion action:

- `Prefill-bound -> add prefill capacity`
- `Decode-bound -> add decode capacity`
- `Decode-KV-bound -> add decode-side KV capacity / tier`

The key point is that this would make PD more adaptive without changing the core PD architecture.

## Suggested First Scope

A practical first step might be:

- expose structured runtime pressure signals
- classify bottlenecks into `Prefill-bound`, `Decode-bound`, or `Decode-KV-bound`
- support one minimal expansion hook or policy target

Even just that would already make PD more adaptive, without requiring full runtime elasticity.

## Non-Goals

This is **not** proposing:

- replacing PD disaggregation
- generic runtime GPU hot-plug
- runtime TP/NCCL topology mutation within an active worker group
- full cluster autoscaling inside vLLM

## Related Work

This seems closely related to, but different from, the following threads:

- PD disaggregation roadmap: #33702
- KV transfer push-model discussion: #36923
- KV cache offloading RFC: #19854
- Multi-tier offloading RFC: #38260
- NIXL handshake / autoscaling decode discussion: #19777

My understanding is that those efforts already provide the right building blocks. What seems missing is a policy/runtime layer that decides which side should be expanded first when pressure emerges inside an already disaggregated deployment.

## Questions

I would really appreciate feedback on a few points:

- does this direction fit the current PD roadmap?
- which bottleneck class would be the best first target?
- should a first step focus only on signaling, or include one minimal expansion hook?
- how should this interact with ongoing KV transfer / request migration work?

title: [RFC]: Add Gumiho speculative decoding to vLLM
body:
### Motivation.

<!--
Open at: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/new?template=750-RFC.yml
Title:   [RFC]: Add Gumiho speculative decoding to vLLM
Labels:  RFC (added automatically by the template)

Paste each section below into the matching field of the RFC template.
-->

## Motivation.

[Gumiho](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10135) (ICML 2025) is a hybrid speculative
decoding drafter:

1. The first two speculative tokens are produced autoregressively by an
   EAGLE-style transformer head.
2. Every additional speculative token is produced **in parallel** by per-step
   MLP heads conditioned on the embeddings and hidden states of the first two
   draft tokens.

The motivation is that **early speculative tokens matter more than late
ones**. Each accepted prefix token unlocks all later tokens in the same draft,
so allocating more compute to the first two positions (a small but
high-quality transformer head) and amortising the rest with cheap parallel
MLP heads yields a better acceptance-rate / drafter-latency trade-off than
either a pure EAGLE drafter (all transformer, sequential) or a pure
MLPSpeculator drafter (all MLP, parallel but lower quality).

Concretely, this means a lower per-step drafter latency than EAGLE/EAGLE3
when `num_speculative_tokens > 2`, with similar end-to-end accepted-token
gains.

We have a working ROCm prototype on top of vLLM v0.16.0 and have already
ported it to current `main` with all CI hygiene applied; the changes are
small and contained.

## Proposed Change.

Add `"method": "gumiho"` as a new V1 speculative decoding method.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43544

### Surface

```python
LLM(
    model="meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "gumiho",
        "model": "amd/Gumiho-llama3-8b",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
        "draft_tensor_parallel_size": 1,
    },
)
```

### Implementation

* **New drafter model** `vllm/model_executor/models/gumiho.py`
  (`GumihoLlamaForCausalLM` + inner `GumihoLlamaModel` + `GumihoResBlock`,
  `GumihoNoResBlock`, weight loader). The transformer head reuses
  `LlamaDecoderLayer` from `llama_eagle.py` exactly like EAGLE does.
* **New proposer** `vllm/v1/spec_decode/gumiho.py`
  (`GumihoProposer(EagleProposer)`). Only overrides two new hooks defined on
  `SpecDecodeBaseProposer`:

  | Hook | Default | Gumiho |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `_init_draft_hidden_states_list` | returns `None` | returns `[sample_hidden_states]` so the sequential loop also collects hidden states |
  | `_maybe_get_mlp_draft_token_ids` | returns `None` | after the 2nd draft step, calls `GumihoLlamaForCausalLM.generate_mlp_draft_token_ids(...)` and short-circuits the rest of the loop |

  Both hooks are no-ops in the base class, so existing proposers
  (EAGLE / EAGLE3 / MTP / DFlash / draft_model / ...) are not affected.

* **New HF config wrapper** `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/gumiho.py`
  (`GumihoConfig`), mirroring how `EAGLEConfig` wraps the underlying Llama
  backbone.

* **Wiring**
  * `SpeculativeConfig`: add `gumiho` to `SpeculativeMethod`, `use_eagle()`,
    the draft-TP=1 forced set, the model-type auto-detect path, and add a
    config-wrap branch parallel to the EAGLE one (reusing the existing
    `update_arch_()` helper).
  * `gpu_model_runner.GPUModelRunner.__init__`: add a `method == "gumiho"`
    branch matched **before** `use_eagle()` so we don't fall back to a plain
    `EagleProposer`.
  * `v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py`: raise an explicit
    `NotImplementedError` on the V2 GPU runner.
  * Model + HF-config registry entries.

* **Docs + example** under
  `docs/features/speculative_decoding/gumiho.md` and a new
  `--method gumiho` branch in
  `examples/features/speculative_decoding/spec_decode_offline.py`.

* **Unit tests** under `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_gumiho.py` (CPU-only,
  exercises `GumihoConfig`, MLP-head shape contract, OOB-head filtering, and
  the two hooks).

### Out of scope for the first PR

These can come as follow-ups once the basic path is merged and reviewed:

* **Tree attention / FTA**: the reference Gumiho training code uses an FTA
  tree for verification. The V1 verifier currently does not support tree
  drafts, so this PR uses the standard linear-chain V1 verifier.
* **Probabilistic draft sampling**: the MLP heads currently produce argmax
  ids only; with `draft_sample_method=probabilistic` we fall back to the
  sequential transformer path. Adding logits output to the MLP heads is a
  small, follow-up change.
* **V2 GPU model runner** path.
* **Multimodal drafters**.

### Diff size

* 5 new files: `vllm/v1/spec_decode/gumiho.py` (74 LoC),
  `vllm/model_executor/models/gumiho.py` (437 LoC),
  `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/gumiho.py` (80 LoC),
  `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_gumiho.py` (350 LoC),
  `docs/features/speculative_decoding/gumiho.md` (72 LoC).
* 9 modified files: net +110 / -4 LoC.

The PR with the full diff is at <!-- TODO: link your PR URL once opened -->.

## Feedback Period.

Two weeks (we'd like to keep the review loop short since the diff is
contained and we have a working prototype, but happy to extend if a
maintainer raises larger design questions).

## CC List.

@WoosukKwon @LiuXiaoxuanPKU @ekagra-ranjan
<!--
TODO before submitting:
* Look at recent EAGLE / MTP / DFlash PRs and CC their reviewers as well,
  e.g. `git log --oneline -- vllm/v1/spec_decode/` on main to find them.
-->

## Any Other Things.

* Paper: Li et al., [_Gumiho: A Hybrid Architecture to Prioritize Early
  Tokens in Speculative Decoding_](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10135), **ICML
  2025**.
* Reference code: <https://github.com/AMD-AIG-AIMA/Gumiho>.
* Pre-trained drafter: <https://huggingface.co/amd/Gumiho-llama3-8b>.
* This RFC is submitted by the original authors of the paper.
* Smoke-test on ROCm shows the V1 path is producing accepted tokens end-to-end
  (mean acceptance length ≈ 1.67 on a small 16-prompt eval with
  `num_speculative_tokens=3`); we'll post a full benchmark vs. EAGLE3 along
  with the PR.


### Proposed Change.

title: MLA: kv_b_proj.weight.dtype AttributeError on quantized ColumnParallelLinear in chunked prefill
body:
## Description

When using a quantized (AWQ/GPTQ/compressed-tensors) model with MLA attention, vLLM crashes with an `AttributeError` during chunked prefill because `kv_b_proj` is a `ColumnParallelLinear` that lacks a `.weight` attribute after quantization.

## Error

```
AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

at `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:2094` in `_compute_prefill_context`:

```python
kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype)
```

## Root Cause

Lines 2084-2087 already correctly handle quantized layers:

```python
_kv_b_proj_w_dtype = (
    self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype
    if hasattr(self.kv_b_proj, "weight")
    else self.kv_b_proj.params_dtype
)
```

But line 2094 ignores `_kv_b_proj_w_dtype` and directly accesses `self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype` without the `hasattr` guard.

## Fix

On line 2094, replace:

```python
kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype)
```

with:

```python
kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(_kv_b_proj_w_dtype)
```

The variable `_kv_b_proj_w_dtype` is already computed with the correct `hasattr` guard immediately above.

## Impact

vLLM EngineCore crashes with a fatal error, forcing a full restart (service enters crash loop under load). All inflight requests fail with HTTP 500.

## Environment

- vLLM version: v0.21.1rc1.dev384 (nightly, also present in current main)
- Model: GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit (quantized with compressed-tensors)
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3090 (CUDA 12.9)
- Quantization: compressed-tensors (AWQ group_size=32, num_bits=4)
- CUDA graphs: enabled
- MLA: enabled (model uses Multi-head Latent Attention)

## Stack Trace

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 2094, in _compute_prefill_context
    kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype)
                                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

title: [Feature][ModelOpt]: Support NVFP4_AWQ checkpoints with native NVFP4 linear kernels
body:
### Feature request

The existing ModelOpt integration mainly supports FP8 and standard NVFP4. This is not sufficient for some quality-sensitive models.

For example, standard ModelOpt NVFP4 causes significant quality degradation on Cosmos3. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/4337

Need  vLLM to support more ModelOpt quantization methods, including:

- ModelOpt NVFP4_AWQ
- ModelOpt NVFP4_SVDQUANT
- More new ModelOpt quantization methods in the future

title: [RFC]: Adaptive Speculation Depth for MoE Models via Per-Iteration Utility Budgeting
body:
### Motivation.

Speculative decoding with a static `num_speculative_tokens` causes measurable
throughput **regressions** on MoE models (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-MoE, Kimi-K2,
Mixtral, etc.). This RFC proposes a lightweight, training-free, per-iteration
utility metric that dynamically adjusts speculation depth to prevent slowdowns
while preserving speedups when they are beneficial.

### The core problem: draft trees over-activate MoE experts

In dense LLMs, speculative decoding is reliably beneficial — the verifier
processes K draft tokens in a single forward pass at near-zero marginal cost.
For MoE models, this assumption breaks down.

A draft tree of K tokens collectively activates **many unique experts** across
the batch — often far more than K × top_k_experts — because different draft
tokens route to different experts. This causes:

1. **Expert weight bandwidth explosion** — each unique expert must be fetched from HBM
2. **EP all-to-all volume increase** — more unique destination ranks per step
3. **Verification time scaling with unique experts**, not just token count

Recent empirical results quantify this regression:

| Static K | Unique experts vs K=0 | Verification overhead | Net throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~1.3× | 1.1× | +10% |
| 4 | ~3.2× | 1.9× | −15% (slowdown) |
| 8 | ~6.1× | 2.4× | **−35% (severe slowdown)** |

The [Cascade paper (arXiv:2506.20675)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675)
implements an adaptive K controller in vLLM and shows that static K=4 causes
**up to 1.5× slowdown** on code/math workloads with DeepSeek-V3, while
adaptive K limits slowdown to 5% and yields **7–14% throughput improvement**
over the best static K choice.

This aligns directly with the Q2 2026 roadmap goal of
["composable speculation"](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39749)
and the active tracking issue
[#28947](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28947).

### Proposed Change.


### Core idea: per-iteration speculation utility as a dynamic K controller

Define **speculation utility** U at each decoding step as:

```
U = accepted_tokens_this_step / expert_activation_overhead_this_step
```

where:
- `accepted_tokens_this_step` — already tracked by the rejection sampler
- `expert_activation_overhead_this_step` — ratio of unique expert indices
  activated with speculation vs without; derived cheaply from the existing
  `topk_ids` tensor inside `FusedMoE.forward()` (zero additional compute)

**Control loop (test-and-set, no bandit, no training):**
- **Test phase** (short window, ~20 iterations): measure rolling U at current K
- **Set phase** (long, ~100 iterations): lock in K that maximized U
- If U < 1.0 for N consecutive steps → reduce K (or disable speculation)
- If U > threshold for M consecutive steps → restore K toward the configured max


### Codebase changes

**1. `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/` — `FusedMoE.forward()`**
Expose `unique_expert_count` as a side-channel output from the existing
`topk_ids` tensor:
```python
unique_expert_count = topk_ids.unique().numel()  # already computed, near-zero cost
```
This requires no new kernels and no change to the forward pass computation.

**2. `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` — new `MoESpecUtilityTracker` class**
```python
class MoESpecUtilityTracker:
    def update(self, accepted: int, unique_experts: int) -> None: ...
    def recommended_k(self, max_k: int) -> int: ...
    def reset(self) -> None: ...
```
Stateless across requests; operates on iteration-level aggregates.

**3. `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` — scheduler integration**
Wire `recommended_k()` into the step that sets `num_speculative_tokens` for
the next iteration. The adapted K is bounded by the user-configured max.

**4. `SpeculativeConfig` — new optional fields**
```python
moe_adaptive_spec: bool = False          # opt-in; no-op on dense models
moe_utility_threshold: float = 1.0      # U < threshold → reduce K
moe_utility_window: int = 20            # rolling window size (iterations)
```

**5. Telemetry (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/metrics.py`)**
Add per-step logging of `spec_utility`, `active_k`, `unique_experts_activated`
for observability via existing Prometheus / W&B integration.

### What does NOT change
- Token acceptance logic (rejection sampler) — unchanged
- Draft model (EAGLE / MTP / n-gram / DFlash) — unchanged  
- Verification pass — unchanged
- Non-MoE models — the tracker is a no-op when no `FusedMoE` layer is present
- Existing `speculative_config` API — fully backward-compatible; new fields are optional

### Example API (no breaking change)
```python
llm = LLM(
    model="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "mtp",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 4,   # upper bound; adapted downward at runtime
        "moe_adaptive_spec": True,
        "moe_utility_threshold": 1.0,
        "moe_utility_window": 20,
    },
)
```

### Open questions for discussion

1. **Where to compute `unique_expert_count`?** Preferred: inside
   `FusedMoE.forward()` from the existing `topk_ids` — zero overhead.
   Alternative: post-hoc from telemetry logs (higher latency, less useful).

2. **Discrete vs continuous K adaptation?** Cascade uses discrete
   K ∈ {0, 1, 2, 4}. Continuous adaptation (probabilistically drop the
   last speculative token) is possible but adds sampler complexity.

3. **Interaction with EPLB?** EPLB already rebalances experts across EP ranks.
   Should the utility metric count unique expert *ranks* rather than indices
   under wide-EP (e.g. 64-way EP for DeepSeek-V3)?

4. **Scheduler vs model-runner level?** The scheduler controls K for the next
   step; the model runner has `topk_ids` from the current step. A one-step
   feedback loop is simplest. Is this the right boundary?

5. **Interaction with MTP > 1 spec token for DeepSeek V3.2**
   (see [#31845](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31845)) —
   should adaptive K take priority over or compose with the MTP-specific
   per-model limits?

### Implementation plan (if RFC accepted)

- [ ] Add `unique_expert_count` instrumentation to `FusedMoE.forward()` (non-breaking)
- [ ] Implement `MoESpecUtilityTracker` with unit tests
- [ ] Wire `recommended_k()` into the spec-decode scheduler
- [ ] Add `moe_adaptive_spec` to `SpeculativeConfig` with documentation
- [ ] Benchmark on DeepSeek-V3 + MTP and Qwen3-MoE + EAGLE; report
  utility distributions and throughput vs static K baselines
- [ ] Gate behind flag, disabled by default, for safe rollout


### Feedback Period.

2 weeks

### CC List.

@benchislett  @mgoin  @fynnsu  @WoosukKwon @simon-mo

### Any Other Things.

### Prior art

| Work | Relevance |
|---|---|
| [Cascade (arXiv:2506.20675)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675) | Adaptive K in vLLM; 7–14% throughput gains on MoE |
| [MoE-Spec (arXiv:2602.16052)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16052) | Expert budgeting at verification time; training-free |
| [Tracking Issue #28947](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28947) | Spec-decode perf improvements (active) |
| [Q2 2026 Roadmap #39749](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39749) | "Composable speculation" roadmap item |
| [DDTree Feature Request #40809](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40809) | Related new drafting strategy |
| [RFC #45133 — Triton Kernel Dispatcher](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45133) | Related multi-platform kernel dispatch RFC |

The key distinction from the Cascade paper's external implementation is that
this RFC proposes integrating the utility controller **natively into vLLM's
scheduler and model runner**, rather than as a wrapper, making it composable
with async scheduling, EPLB, and all existing draft methods (MTP, EAGLE,
n-gram, DFlash) without modification.

title: [Bug]: persistent KV Cache memory not released after benchmark completion
body: ### Your current environment vllm 0.22.0 + mooncakestore connector Observed Behavior: After the benchmark completes, ~40% of the HBM (KV cache) remains allocated and is not immediately released. This persists for at least 20 minutes with no active requests. However, when I start a new benchmark, the memory begins to be released (evicted) to accommodate incoming requests. Expected Behavior: I expected the KV cache to be released promptly after the benchmark finishes, or at least to see a more aggressive eviction policy, especially when there are no pending requests. Questions: Is this behavior expected for MooncakeStoreConnector, or does it indicate a configuration issue? If this is by design, could you explain the rationale behind keeping the cache warm for such a long duration even when no requests are being served? Are there any configuration parameters (e.g., max_num_seqs, gpu_memory_utilization, or connector-specific flags) that can be tuned to achieve more proactive memory release after workload completion? I would appreciate any guidance or clarification on whether this is a known behavior or a potential bug. The fact that memory only starts releasing during the next benchmark suggests a lazy eviction policy, but I want to confirm if this is the intended design. Thank you for your time! ### 🐛 Describe the bug try again , same phenomenon ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: test_tp_language_generation[Llama-3.2-1B-...parallel_setup{9,10}] times out (480s) on Hopper — server actually starts but exceeds the test deadline
body:
### Your current environment

- vllm `0.22.2.dev` (HCF fork at upstream sha `fce03608d`, identical to upstream main on the touched test files — `tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py` has 0-line diff vs `vllm-project/vllm@main`)
- transformers: verified on both `4.57.1` and `5.12.1` (latest stable, released 2026-06-15) — same failure
- 4 × NVIDIA H20 (sm_90), CUDA 13.0, torch `2.11.0+cu130`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py::test_tp_language_generation` collected from `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct: PPTestSettings.detailed()`. Two of the 10 expanded combinations consistently fail on H20:

- `parallel_setup9-mp` → `(tp=2, pp=2, eager_mode=True)` × `mp`
- `parallel_setup10-ray` → `(tp=2, pp=2, eager_mode=True)` × `ray`

(both are the heaviest detailed setup: tp=2 pp=2 = 4 GPU.)

Stack:
```
tests/utils.py:273: self._wait_for_server(url=self.url_for("health"), timeout=max_wait_seconds)
...
E   RuntimeError: Server failed to start in time.
tests/utils.py:652: RuntimeError
```

### Reproducer

```bash
pytest -v -p no:rerunfailures \
    "tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py::test_tp_language_generation[meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-parallel_setup9-mp-auto-test_options9]" \
    "tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py::test_tp_language_generation[meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-parallel_setup10-ray-auto-test_options10]"
```

Total wall-clock 16:56s. Both fail with the timeout above.

### Diagnosis: it's a deadline issue, not a server-bring-up bug

The vllm server **is starting** for both setups — verified by inspecting the running pytest pod:

- For `setup10-ray`: `vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray ...` was alive for 14+ minutes, all 4 GPUs at 100% utilization, ray gcs and dashboard processes running, model loaded, weights loaded, **CUDA graphs (decode, FULL) finished capturing** (`100%|██████████| 4/4`). At that point the test process gives up because:

```python
# tests/utils.py:271
max_wait_seconds = max_wait_seconds or 480   # 8 minutes
```

`tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py:_compare_tp` does not override `max_wait_seconds`, so the default 480s applies. Llama-3.2-1B + tp=2 pp=2 + Ray executor on H20 takes longer than 480s to reach `/health` 200 (cold flashinfer autotune + cuda graph capture across 4 workers).

Earlier setups (`setup3` ... `setup8`, `setup11`, `setup12`) finish within 480s on the same node, so the deadline is just barely too tight for the heaviest detailed combos when the cluster is under any contention.

### Suggested directions (no preference, just listing)

1. Bump `_compare_tp`'s call-site timeout (e.g. pass `max_wait_seconds=900` to `compare_two_settings`) for distributed pipeline tests where init dominates.
2. Bump the global `max_wait_seconds or 480` default in `tests/utils.py` to `or 900` (or read from an env var).
3. Skip these specific parametrize cells on Hopper if they can be considered redundant with cheaper setups.

Filing this as a report — happy to put up a PR for whichever direction maintainers prefer.

title: [ROCm][Perf] ROCM_ATTN selected over ROCM_AITER_FA for MHA decode despite VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 (CDNA)
body:
### Summary

On CDNA (MI300X/MI325X/MI355X), setting `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` for an MHA model does **not** result in `ROCM_AITER_FA` being selected for decode attention — vLLM still picks the non-AITER `ROCM_ATTN`. This contradicts the documented behavior and the published benchmarks, and significantly slows attention-heavy paths (notably speculative decoding).

### Root cause

In `vllm/platforms/rocm.py::_get_backend_priorities()`, `ROCM_ATTN` is appended to the candidate list **before** `ROCM_AITER_FA`. Selection picks the lowest-index valid backend, so `ROCM_ATTN` wins whenever it is valid — even when the operator explicitly enabled AITER and `ROCM_AITER_FA` is valid.

Server log (AITER is otherwise active — MoE/FP8/sampler all use AITER):
```
[rocm.py] Found incompatible backend(s) [TURBOQUANT] with AttentionType.DECODER.
Overriding with ROCM_ATTN out of potential backends:
['ROCM_ATTN', 'ROCM_AITER_FA', 'ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN', 'TRITON_ATTN'].
```

This is inconsistent with the [vLLM ROCm attention-backend blog](https://blog.vllm.ai/2026/02/27/rocm-attention-backend.html): *"With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, vLLM automatically selects `ROCM_AITER_FA` for MHA models."* In practice it does not.

### Impact (measured, 8x MI300X)

`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct-FP8`, EAGLE3 speculative decoding, real (padded) MMMU prompts, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. `ROCM_AITER_FA` selected via `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA`; everything else identical to the default-selection run.

**SD decode TPOT (ms) — default selection vs ROCM_AITER_FA:**

| mc | v0.21 default | v0.21 AITER_FA | v0.22 default | v0.22 AITER_FA | v0.23 default | v0.23 AITER_FA |
|----|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| 1  | 11.10 | **5.62** | 10.36 | **5.29** | 10.65 | **5.31** |
| 4  | 14.64 | **7.02** | 14.49 | **6.60** | 13.89 | **6.60** |
| 8  | 18.92 | **8.58** | 18.94 | **8.31** | 18.64 | **8.24** |
| 16 | 24.23 | **11.73** | 22.02 | **11.74** | 24.67 | **11.12** |

**SD throughput (tok/s):**

| mc | v0.21 default | v0.21 AITER_FA | v0.23 default | v0.23 AITER_FA |
|----|------|------|------|------|
| 1  | 87  | **178** | 89  | **197** |
| 8  | 390 | **808** | 393 | **798** |
| 16 | 416 | **1083** | 399 | **1023** |

Non-speculative baseline decode is unchanged within noise (±1–5%), consistent with the blog's finding that `ROCM_ATTN`'s HIP paged-decode kernel falls back to Triton only for unsupported KV head sizes (e.g. Qwen3-VL-235B) — which the SD draft+verify loop hits hardest. The blog reports `ROCM_AITER_FA` is **2.8–4.6× faster TPOT / 2.7–4.4× higher throughput** than `ROCM_ATTN` for MHA on CDNA3 (MI300X).

### Proposed fix

Reorder `_get_backend_priorities()` so `ROCM_AITER_FA` outranks `ROCM_ATTN` **only when `is_mha_enabled()` is true** (env opt-in + gfx9). Radeon/RDNA and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=0` are unaffected (`is_mha_enabled()` is False there); `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` keeps its original position; the KV-connector exclusion of `ROCM_ATTN` is preserved.

PR: fix in progress (linked below). Scope is intentionally narrow — this is **not** "make AITER the global default" (which would regress Radeon and was the scope of the now-closed #21805 / #21366); it only honors an explicit opt-in.

### Related
- #39965 — sibling ROCm default-selection regression (ROCM_ATTN vs Triton, prefill)
- #21805 / #21366 — broader auto-select RFC + impl, both closed/unmerged; this is a much smaller targeted fix
- #33163 — AITER env-var consolidation

### Environment
- 8x AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942 / CDNA3), ROCm 7.x
- vLLM v0.21.0 / v0.22.0 / v0.23.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` images); logic unchanged on current `main`
- `VLLM_USE_V1=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On macOS arm64 with the CPU backend, Qwen3.5-0.8B crashes when `mamba_cache_mode="align"` needs to copy Mamba/GDN state across blocks and Triton is unavailable.

The failing line is in `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`:

```python
batch_memcpy_kernel[grid](src_ptrs, dst_ptrs, sizes, BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE)
```

When Triton is not installed/available on this CPU setup, `batch_memcpy_kernel` behaves like a normal Python function rather than a Triton launchable object, so the `[...]` launch syntax raises:

```text
TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable
```

I hit this while running vLLM with an external KV connector (LMCache), but the crash is in vLLM's Mamba align preprocessing path after scheduling a request that crosses the Mamba/attention block boundary. A short prompt works; a prompt of ~732 tokens triggers the copy path. In this run vLLM logs:

```text
Setting attention block size to 640 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.
Padding mamba page size by 20.75% to ensure that mamba page size and attention page size are exactly equal.
```

Command shape used:

```bash

export VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=nobind
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export KMP_BLOCKTIME=0
export VLLM_HOST_IP=127.0.0.1
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo0
export VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1

vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B/snapshot \
  --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B \
  --port 18000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 1200 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 1073741824 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1279 \
  --language-model-only \
  --skip-mm-profiling \
  --enforce-eager
```

Request shape that crossed the 640-token boundary:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:18000/v1/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model":"Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B",
    "prompt":"Summarize in one short sentence.\n'"$(python3 - <<'PY'
print('cache test. ' * 240, end='')
PY
)"'\nAnswer:",
    "max_tokens":8,
    "temperature":0
  }'
```

Full relevant traceback:

```text
WorkerProc hit an exception.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../site-packages/vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 992, in worker_busy_loop
    output = func(*args, **kwargs)
  File ".../site-packages/vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 351, in execute_model
    return self.worker.execute_model(scheduler_output)
  File ".../site-packages/torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 124, in decorate_context
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
  File ".../site-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 896, in execute_model
    output = self.model_runner.execute_model(
  File ".../site-packages/torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 124, in decorate_context
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
  File ".../site-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 4218, in execute_model
    mamba_utils.preprocess_mamba(
  File ".../site-packages/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 741, in preprocess_mamba
    do_mamba_copy_block(copy_bufs)
  File ".../site-packages/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 653, in do_mamba_copy_block
    batch_memcpy(
  File ".../site-packages/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 221, in batch_memcpy
    batch_memcpy_kernel[grid](src_ptrs, dst_ptrs, sizes, BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE)
TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable
```

A local workaround was to add a CPU fallback in `batch_memcpy` when `batch_memcpy_kernel` is not launchable, using `ctypes.memmove` for each `(src_ptr, dst_ptr, size)`. With that fallback, the same two 732-token completion requests succeeded on the same host.

```python
if not hasattr(batch_memcpy_kernel, "__getitem__"):
    src_ptrs_cpu = src_ptrs.detach().cpu().tolist()
    dst_ptrs_cpu = dst_ptrs.detach().cpu().tolist()
    sizes_cpu = sizes.detach().cpu().tolist()
    for src, dst, size in zip(src_ptrs_cpu, dst_ptrs_cpu, sizes_cpu):
        ctypes.memmove(int(dst), int(src), int(size))
    return
```

Expected behavior: CPU/macOS execution should either use a CPU copy fallback for Mamba state copies when Triton is unavailable, or fail earlier with a clear unsupported-configuration error instead of crashing the engine at request time.

title: [RFC]: Compact candidate-set renormalization for native top-k/top-p sampling
body:
### Motivation.

## Motivation

  I would like to discuss a native sampling optimization for the `top_k` / `top_p` path.

  In the current native sampler, the common flow is:

  1. apply top-k / top-p filtering over the full vocabulary;
  2. compute full-vocab softmax;
  3. sample from the full-vocab probability tensor.

  For top-k and top-k+top-p decoding, most vocabulary entries are guaranteed to have zero probability after filtering. That means the later renormalization and sampling work can be done directly on
  the surviving candidate set instead of the full vocabulary.

  The proposed optimization is:

  1. select the surviving candidates;
  2. renormalize only those candidates;
  3. sample from the compact candidate distribution;
  4. map the sampled candidate back to the original vocab id.

  This avoids full-vocab masking + full-vocab softmax + full-vocab sampling work in the common top-k / top-k+top-p case.

  ## Sampling parameters

  The relevant sampling parameters are:

  - `top_k`:
    - integer cap on how many candidates are kept per row;
    - if active, only the highest-scoring `top_k` tokens remain eligible.
  - `top_p`:
    - nucleus threshold in cumulative probability space;
    - if active, tokens are kept until the cumulative probability reaches the threshold.
  - both can be used together:
    - first apply top-k to restrict the candidate set;
    - then apply top-p inside that surviving candidate set.

  In this proposal, the fast path targets:
  - top-k only
  - top-k + top-p

  ## Scope

  The proposed fast path applies when:

  - `k is not None`
  - active top-k is enabled for all rows, i.e. `k < vocab_size`
  - processed logits/logprobs are not requested

  I would not claim pure top-p-only support in this fast path, because exact pure top-p still needs identifying the nucleus over the full vocabulary unless a different exact algorithm is introduced.

  ## Correctness

  This optimization does not change the sampling mathematics.

  The baseline path computes:

  ```text
  softmax(mask_top_k_top_p(logits))
  ```

  where tokens outside the surviving set get zero probability.

  The candidate path computes the same distribution over the surviving candidates only:
  
  ```text
  softmax(logits[surviving_candidate_indices])
  ```

  and then gathers the sampled candidate back to the original vocabulary id.

  So this changes the computation layout, not the decoding semantics.

  I verified this by comparing the full-vocab masked probability tensor against the candidate-renormalized probability tensor:
  
  ```text
  top-k       distribution_match=True  max_abs_diff=2.980e-08
  top-k+top-p distribution_match=True  max_abs_diff=1.490e-08
  ```

  I also checked that sampled tokens always fall within the same surviving candidate set:

  ```text
  top-k       sampled_in_surviving_set=True
  top-k+top-p sampled_in_surviving_set=True
  ```

  The probability softmax remains fp32, matching the current native path. The existing random_sample implementation is reused, including the use_fp64_gumbel behavior.

  One note: sampled token ids are not guaranteed to be bitwise identical for the same global RNG seed, because the optimized path draws random noise only for surviving candidates instead of all
  vocabulary entries. The intended guarantee is distributional equivalence, not identical RNG consumption.

  ## Preliminary performance

  Tested on latest vLLM origin/main at commit 6f3da46, NVIDIA H100 PCIe, PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124.

  Baseline:

  top_k:  sampled from [1, 63]
  top_p: 1.0
  logits dtype: fp32

  latest-main apply_top_k_top_p
  (Triton when batch >= 8)
  + full-vocab softmax
  + random_sample

  Results:

  ``` text
   batch    vocab  baseline_ms candidate_ms  speedup
       1    32768        0.181        0.211     0.86x
       4    32768        0.204        0.203     1.01x
      16    32768        0.356        0.202     1.76x
      64    32768        0.359        0.201     1.79x
     256    32768        0.944        0.265     3.57x
    1024    32768        2.783        0.794     3.50x

       1   131072        0.208        0.202     1.03x
       4   131072        0.258        0.200     1.29x
      16   131072        1.217        0.201     6.04x
      64   131072        1.306        0.261     5.01x
     256   131072        4.469        0.785     5.69x
    1024   131072       14.617        2.277     6.42x
  ```
  The benefit is most visible for larger batch sizes and larger vocabularies. For very small batches the fast path can be neutral or slightly slower.

  ## Questions

  1. Does this candidate-set renormalization fast path make sense for the native sampler?
  2. Should the fast path be guarded by a batch-size or vocab-size threshold?
  3. Is torch.all(k < vocab_size) an acceptable guard, or should sampler metadata expose whether all requests have active top-k?
  4. Should this be implemented first as a small PyTorch-native fast path, or as a dedicated Triton kernel?

### Proposed Change.

## Proposed Change

  Add a native candidate-set fast path for top-k / top-k+top-p sampling.

  The fast path would:
  1. select the top-k candidates for each row;
  2. optionally apply top-p within the surviving top-k set;
  3. renormalize only the surviving candidates;
  4. sample from that compact distribution;
  5. map the sampled candidate back to the original vocabulary id.

  This path should only be enabled when:
  - `k is not None`
  - active top-k is enabled for all rows
  - processed logits/logprobs are not requested

  The fallback path should remain unchanged for all other cases.

  I also added tests to verify:
  - the candidate-set probability distribution matches the masked full-vocab distribution;
  - sampled tokens always belong to the surviving candidate set.

title: [Bug]: MLA indexer block_table shape mismatch when max_model_len is auto-reduced after InputBatch creation
body:
### Your current environment

## Your current environment

- **vLLM version**: v0.23.0
- **GPU**: NVIDIA H20 
- **Python**: 3.12
- **OS**: Linux
- **Attention backend**: FlashMLA (block_size=64)
- **Model**: GLM-5.1 (or any MLA-based model: GLM-5/5.2, DeepSeek-V2/V3)
- **Configuration**: TP + DP + EP with MTP speculative decoding enabled

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

When running MLA models with MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculative decoding, and the engine auto-reduces `max_model_len` to fit available GPU memory, a `RuntimeError` occurs during the decode phase:

```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (2464) must match the existing size (3168)
at non-singleton dimension 1. Target sizes: [51, 2464]. Tensor sizes: [51, 3168]
```

The MLA indexer's `expanded_block_table_buffer` is allocated with fewer columns than the `InputBatch.block_table` because `InputBatch` was created **before** `max_model_len` was reduced, and it is never rebuilt afterward.

## Root Cause Analysis

The initialization sequence in `GPUModelRunner` has a timing issue between `InputBatch` creation and `max_model_len` auto-reduction:

### Timeline

1. **`GPUModelRunner.__init__()`** creates `InputBatch` with the **original** `max_model_len` (e.g., 202,752):
   ```python
   # block_table columns = cdiv(202752, 64) = 3168
   self.input_batch = InputBatch(...)
   ```

2. **Engine detects insufficient GPU memory** and calls `update_max_model_len(157696)` to auto-reduce the value.

3. **`initialize_kv_cache()` → `initialize_metadata_builders()`** creates the MLA indexer with the **new** `max_model_len`:
   ```python
   # expanded_block_table_buffer columns = cdiv(157696, 64) = 2464
   ```

4. **`may_reinitialize_input_batch()`** is called but only checks:
   ```python
   if (
       block_sizes != self._init_block_sizes        # False (both [64])
       or kernel_block_sizes != self._init_kernel_block_sizes  # False
   ):
   ```
   It does **NOT** check whether `max_model_len` has changed.

5. Since the condition is not triggered, `InputBatch` is **NOT rebuilt**, retaining the stale `block_table` with **3168 columns**.

6. During decode, `torch.repeat_interleave` tries to expand `block_table[N, 3168]` into the indexer buffer `[max_num_batched_tokens, 2464]` → **RuntimeError**.

### Why the existing checks miss this case

`may_reinitialize_input_batch()` guards against changes in `block_size` or `kernel_block_size`, but when `max_model_len` is reduced without changing the block size (FlashMLA always uses block_size=64), neither check fires.

## Steps to Reproduce

**Trigger conditions** (all must be met simultaneously):

1. Use an MLA attention backend (FlashMLA with `block_size=64`)
2. Enable MTP speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens >= 1`)
3. Use a configuration that causes high memory pressure (e.g., DP + EP), forcing the engine to auto-reduce `max_model_len`
4. The auto-reduction must NOT change `block_size` (always the case for FlashMLA)
5. Send enough requests to enter the decode phase

**Example launch configuration**:

```bash
vllm serve GLM-5.1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8999  --max-model-len auto --trust-remote-code --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

With insufficient GPU memory to support `max_model_len=202752`, the engine auto-reduces it (e.g., to 157696). The crash occurs on the first decode step.

## Proposed Fix

Add a `max_model_len` change check in `may_reinitialize_input_batch()`:

```python
def may_reinitialize_input_batch(self):
    ...
    if (
        block_sizes != self._init_block_sizes
        or kernel_block_sizes != self._init_kernel_block_sizes
        or max_model_len != self.input_batch.max_model_len  # <-- Add this check
    ):
        self.input_batch = InputBatch(
            ...
        )
        ...
```

This ensures `InputBatch` is rebuilt whenever `max_model_len` changes, keeping `block_table` column count consistent with the MLA indexer's `expanded_block_table_buffer`.

title: MTP + MLA: slot_mapping assert fails with list[dict] from ubatch slicing
body:
## Bug: `Expected slot_mapping to be a dict, got <class 'list'>`

### Environment
- vLLM nightly `0.23.1rc1.dev471+ge312c5cb2`
- NVIDIA H200 GPUs, EP16 (2 nodes × 8 GPUs)
- Model: GLM-5.2-FP8 (753B MoE) with MLA (DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER / FLASHMLA_SPARSE)
- MTP speculative decoding: `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`
- All2all backend: `deepep_low_latency`

### Description

During KV cache initialization, MTP creates ubatch slices that cause `slot_mapping` to be returned as `list[dict[str, torch.Tensor]]` instead of `dict[str, torch.Tensor]`. Both `mla_attention.py` and `attention.py` assert that `slot_mapping` is a dict, causing a crash.

The `attn_metadata` handling 10 lines above already handles this exact pattern correctly (list vs dict), but the same handling was not applied to `slot_mapping`.

### Traceback

```
File "vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 133, in __init__
    kv_cache_config = self._initialize_kv_caches(vllm_config)
File "vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 321, in _initialize_kv_caches
    self.model_executor.initialize_from_config(kv_cache_configs)
File "vllm/v1/executor/abstract.py", line 124, in initialize_from_config
    compilation_times: list[CompilationTimes] = self.collective_rpc(
File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 391, in get_response
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Expected slot_mapping to be a dict, got <class 'list'>. '
```

### Root Cause

Introduced in commit b4a6f26c (`[ROCm][perf] Use workspace manager for sparse indexer allocations`, PR #41002) which created `mla_attention.py` as shared code with the strict assert, without accounting for the MTP ubatch `list[dict]` case.

### Affected Files

- `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py` (line 583)
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py` (line 706)

### Suggested Fix

Apply the same pattern already used for `attn_metadata` (lines 572-577 in `mla_attention.py`, lines 695-700 in `attention.py`):

```python
# mla_attention.py, after line 581:
slot_mapping = forward_context.slot_mapping
if isinstance(slot_mapping, list):
    slot_mapping = slot_mapping[0]

# attention.py, after line 705:
slot_mapping = forward_context.slot_mapping
if isinstance(slot_mapping, list):
    slot_mapping = slot_mapping[0]
```

title: [CI] test_mtp_sharded_sampling_equivalence diverges intermittently (2 failures on 2026-09-24)
body:
## What

`tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py::test_mtp_sharded_sampling_equivalence` asserts **bit-exact** equivalence between batch-sharded and replicated sampling under MTP spec decode. It failed twice on main on 2026-09-24:

- [#90930](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90930#01a0d32a-0fd0-4df0-a39f-62346e17d931) — seeded: 2/20 prompts diverged at [12, 17]
- [#91104](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91104#01a0d5e8-707f-4043-8456-b1b525e1efb8) — greedy: 1/20 prompts diverged at [16]

## Regression angle (checked)

- The lane passed at bbd7c24d (build #90915), which already includes the FlashInfer 0.7.0 upgrade (#58069).
- The pass→fail windows contain only XPU/frontend/CPU commits — nothing touching GPU sampling.

So this reads as rare nondeterminism in the MTP sharded-sampling path (kernel scheduling/atomics at logit ties), not a clean commit regression.

## Ask

The test's docstring claims bit-exactness by design. Either the invariant needs a tolerance/narrowing, or there's a real (rare) nondeterminism in the sharded-sampling path worth an owner look. Filing rather than weakening the test unilaterally. cc CI alerts #2268/#2362.

title: [Bug][Spec Decode] num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size + MTP speculator fails full CUDA graph decode capture (InputBatch.make_dummy assert)
body:
### Environment
- vLLM v0.25.0 (official docker image), single H100 NVL 94GB (SM90)
- Target: `prithivMLmods/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-FP8` (compressed-tensors FP8)
- Drafter: `google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized-assistant` (Gemma4 MTP, 4 layers: 3 sliding + 1 full attention)
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` (backend forced due to a separate SM90/SWA selection issue, filed separately)
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` (per the new hint in the downgrade warning, to enable DSD × full CUDA graphs from #45953)

### Repro
```
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve /models \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"/drafter","method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,
    "num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size":[[1,64,3],[65,128,1],[129,512,0]]}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN
```
The env opt-in follows the hint added in 0.25's downgrade warning: *"Overriding cudagraph_mode from FULL_AND_PIECEWISE to PIECEWISE for reliability. Use VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 if you want to use full CUDA graphs."* Without it, DSD falls back to PIECEWISE and does not reach this capture path.

Startup proceeds through weight load, torch.compile, target-model graph capture (`Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL): 150/150` OK), speculator prefill capture OK, then crashes at speculator **decode** FULL capture:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/cudagraph_utils.py", line 83, in create_forward_fn
    attn_state = prepare_inputs_to_capture(
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 604, in prepare_inputs_to_capture
    input_batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_tokens, input_buffers)
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py", line 109, in make_dummy
    assert 0 < num_reqs <= num_tokens
AssertionError
```

### Isolation matrix (3 configurations, same stack otherwise)
| speculative-config | Result |
|---|---|
| DSD table `[[1,64,3],[65,128,1],[129,512,0]]` | crash at ~1% of speculator decode capture |
| DSD table `[[1,64,3],[65,512,1]]` (no K=0 tier) | crash immediately at speculator decode capture |
| static `num_speculative_tokens: 3` (no table) | **capture completes** (`Graph capturing finished`) |

→ The **presence of the batch-size table** is the trigger; K=0 tiers are not required.

### Candidate root cause (hypothesis, file:line trail)
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:205-225` reconstructs per-descriptor decode query lens as
`num_new_sampled_tokens_per_step = decode_query_len − num_speculative_tokens`, an invariant written for the **target** manager (`decode_query_len = K + newly sampled`). The autoregressive speculator's capture manager (`spec_decode/autoregressive/cudagraph_utils.py:59-105`) inherits this base, but MTP drafting has different decode-query semantics (1 token/seq/step), so the derived `num_tokens` collapses to ≈K while `num_reqs` is the capture batch size — matching the observed failure boundary (K=3 table fails from bs=4, K=1 table from bs=2: `num_reqs > num_tokens`). EAGLE presumably passes because its execution shape satisfies the invariant.

### Notes
- The DSD docs state the feature is "only tested with Eagle and Eagle-3"; this report adds the MTP data point. MTP + DSD works on v0.24.0 (runtime K switching across tiers verified with spec-decode counters), but v0.24.0 forces `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` for DSD, so #45953's full-CG path is the reason to move to 0.25 — and this capture bug currently blocks that move for MTP.
- Perf context (v0.24.0, informational, related to #47277): at client concurrency 256 we see DSD mode incur a 12–25% throughput penalty vs no-spec (oscillating run-to-run) with TTFT p50 inflating ~6×, **even with an all-K=0 table producing near-zero draft tokens**. We isolated it away from the cudagraph downgrade (forcing `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` on a no-spec config costs ≈0% at the same concurrency) — the overhead appears to live in the DSD/spec-decode path itself at high batch, matching the "per-step overhead erases the benefit" pattern reported in #47277 on a different stack (Qwen3.5 native MTP / L20X). We can post the isolation trace on that thread once this capture blocker is resolved and we can re-run the comparison on 0.25.
- Workaround today: static `num_speculative_tokens` (on 0.25 the full-CG capture passes; note startup then needs extra gpu-memory-utilization margin — we hit a warmup OOM at 0.95 on a 94GB H100), or DSD on 0.24 with the PIECEWISE cost.

Terminating request. ``` 151645 is `<|im_end|>`, the model's EOS.
