title: [RFC]: Request level text and derender output on `/inference/v1/generate`
body:
### Motivation.

The disaggregated serving path in vLLM is render → generate → derender. `/render` turns an OpenAI request into a `GenerateRequest` (#36166). `/inference/v1/generate` runs it on the GPU tier and returns token IDs (#22817, #24261).
`/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` turn the result back into an OpenAI response (#42729).
This works well for batch and RL traffic where the caller already holds the complete `GenerateResponse`.

Latency sensitive interactive traffic in prefill/decode (P/D) deployments is a poor fit. Streaming derender (#47161) is a stateless per chunk translator, so every SSE chunk from generate costs the client another HTTP round trip:

- One `POST` per chunk with the client echoing `stream_state` back on each call.
- On the parsing path the full `chat_request` is re-sent with every chunk.
- Parser state is rebuilt by replaying all output tokens each chunk. #50550 documents this as O(n³) character work over a generation and defers caching it.

All of this lands on the TPOT critical path and for parsed output the cost grows with response length. A benchmark
of the streaming derender PRs measured it (1×A100-40G, Qwen3-8B, hermes + qwen3 parsers, main plus #50550, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033). At matched load, detokenize and parse on the derender tier cost ~9× the in-process CPU, and E2E p50 rose 15% on multi-thousand-token reasoning outputs. Tokens-in / text-out in a single call already works on the main server (`/v1/completions` accepts token IDs in `prompt`). The gap is specific to deployments whose wire format is `GenerateRequest`.

**Tokenizer availability is per pool. Detokenization is already per request.** Only one of these is a launch time decision:

| | Granularity | Where it's decided today |
|---|---|---|
| Tokenizer loaded | per pool, at launch | `--tokens-only` sets `skip_tokenizer_init` |
| Detokenize this request | per request | `SamplingParams.detokenize`, default `True`. `GenerateRequest.sampling_params` is a full `SamplingParams`, so it's on the wire today. |

The only thing that makes detokenization look launch level is `--tokens-only` overriding the request value. A generate server launched with `--enable-scale-out` and without `--tokens-only` already runs a `FastIncrementalDetokenizer` for every request. The handler then builds the response from `output.token_ids` only and throws `output.text` away.

**P/D makes request level the natural grain:**

- **Only the terminal leg's output reaches the client.** Proxies run the prefill leg with `max_tokens=1` and keep only `kv_transfer_params`. Decode recomputes the last prompt token to sample the first output token itself.
- **Decode already has everything detokenization needs.** `GenerateRequest.token_ids` carries the full prompt and the detokenizer primes its `DecodeStream` from it. No detokenizer state crosses the P→D boundary.
- **State lives with the live request.** `RequestState` owns the detokenizer and is popped on finish and on abort/disconnect. There's no session registry or eviction. That's the property #47161 couldn't get on the stateless derender tier which has no live request to hang state on.
- **No new pool flavor.** P/D fleets already run prefill and decode pools with different launch configs. Prefill pools stay `--tokens-only`. Decode pools load a tokenizer.

This also continues #22817's original design, which says *"We can make `Detokenization` step optional in the `AsyncLLM`"* and sketches a service mapping `GenerateRequest` → `ChatCompletionResponse`.

### Proposed Change.

#### 1. A request-level `output_mode` field

Add a top level field to `GenerateRequest`:

```python
output_mode: Literal["tokens", "text", "derender"] = "tokens"
```

It's a new field rather than a reuse of `sampling_params.detokenize`. That field defaults to `True`, so keying response content off it would change every existing response on tokenizer loaded servers. It's also an engine field and response shape is a serving concern.

| Level | Response adds | Equivalent today | Server needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokens` (default) | nothing, unchanged behavior | `/inference/v1/generate` | nothing |
| `text` | detokenized `text`, resolved logprob tokens | `/v1/completions/derender` | tokenizer |
| `derender` | `content`, `reasoning`, `tool_calls` | `/v1/chat/completions/derender` | tokenizer, parser config, per request parser context |

#### 2. Response shape (proposed, see open question 1)

One response class per level with `GenerateResponse` as a union discriminated on `output_mode` (open question 1, suggested by @DarkLight1337):

```python
class GenerateTokensResponse(GenerateResponseBase):
    output_mode: Literal["tokens"] = "tokens"
    choices: list[GenerateTokensChoice]

class GenerateTextResponse(GenerateResponseBase):
    output_mode: Literal["text"]
    choices: list[GenerateTextChoice]

class GenerateDerenderResponse(GenerateResponseBase):
    output_mode: Literal["derender"]
    choices: list[GenerateDerenderChoice]

GenerateResponse = Annotated[
    Annotated[GenerateTokensResponse, Tag("tokens")]
    | Annotated[GenerateTextResponse, Tag("text")]
    | Annotated[GenerateDerenderResponse, Tag("derender")],
    Discriminator(output_mode_or_tokens),  # missing tag -> "tokens"
]
```

The choices follow the same pattern:

| Level | Choice adds | Stream choice adds | `logprobs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | nothing | nothing | token ID form (#57574) |
| `text` | `text: str` | `text: str` (delta) | resolved token strings (section 5) |
| `derender` | `message: ChatMessage` | `delta: DeltaMessage` | resolved token strings (section 5) |

- **Shared fields stay in the base classes.** `GenerateResponseBase` holds `request_id`, `usage`, `prompt_token_ids`, `mm_placeholders`, `metrics`, `kv_transfer_params` and `ec_transfer_params`. The choice base holds `index`, `finish_reason`, `token_ids`, `routed_experts` and `sampling_mask`. The stream response and stream choices split the same way.
- **The response echoes `output_mode`.** It's what the union discriminates on and it makes every response and stream chunk self-describing. For existing clients this is one new field on `tokens` responses and nothing else changes.
- **A missing `output_mode` means `tokens`.** `GenerateResponse` is also parsed as input by `/derender` (`DerenderChatRequest.generate_response`) and existing clients don't send the field. A plain discriminated union rejects a missing tag, so the discriminator is a callable that falls back to `"tokens"`. The trade-off is that the OpenAPI schema shows a `oneOf` without a discriminator mapping.
- **Mode-specific fields are required, not optional.** `text` is `str` on a text choice and `message` is `ChatMessage` on a derender choice, so callers don't need `None` checks. It also removes the need to exclude unset `text` / `message` / `delta` fields by hand, since the `tokens` classes don't have them.
- **`logprobs` is typed per level.** That answers the question of `choice.logprobs` changing type with `output_mode`. Each level declares its own type.
- **`derender` doesn't carry the raw `text`** which matches `/derender`. `message` / `delta` are the same types `/derender` and `/v1/chat/completions` emit, so the parity check compares field for field.
- **Python code that constructs `GenerateResponse` moves to `GenerateTokensResponse`** because `GenerateResponse` becomes a type alias rather than a class.

Example decode-leg request and stream chunk:

```json
{"token_ids": [151644, 872, ...], "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 512},
 "stream": true, "output_mode": "text", "kv_transfer_params": {...}}
```

```json
{"request_id": "...", "output_mode": "text",
 "choices": [{"index": 0, "token_ids": [9707], "text": " Hello"}]}
```
#### 3. Parser context for the `derender` level (proposed, see open question 2)

Parsers are built per request from context `GenerateRequest` doesn't carry today: `tools`, `tool_choice`, `chat_template_kwargs`. Batch `/derender` solves this by taking the post `adjust_request`
`ChatCompletionRequest`. The proposal mirrors it:

```python
chat_request: ChatCompletionRequest | None = None  # used only when output_mode="derender"
```

- It's sent once per request, not once per chunk as with streaming derender.
- It reuses the batch derender path (`OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat`) and its parity tests with stop string handling added (section 9). That path runs on the renderer's executor which has `renderer_num_workers` threads, default `1`. It runs once per request and decode pools do no prompt tokenization, so contention is low but the pool size caps concurrent `derender` calls.
- Without `chat_request`, a server with a reasoning or tool parser configured returns **400** (section 6). Batch `/derender` falls back to plain detokenization instead which can mix reasoning or tool call markup into `message.content`. Streaming derender already fails closed for parser configured models. Clients that want plain text use `text`. On a server with no parser, `derender` without `chat_request` puts the plain text in `message.content`.

#### 4. Streaming

- **`text`**: `text` carries each chunk's delta from the request's existing incremental detokenizer (`RequestOutputKind.DELTA`). No extra state.
- **`derender`**: one `Parser` per choice, created when the request starts and kept for its lifetime, the same way `/v1/chat/completions` streams today. There's no replay, no `stream_state` and no per chunk `chat_request`.
- **End of stream**: at `text` and `derender` levels, the stream emits a chunk whenever the engine output carries new text or a `finish_reason`, even with no new token IDs. That covers the final output the engine produces on `/abort_requests` which has no token IDs but can flush text held back for stop string matching. The generate stream skips outputs with no new token IDs today (on `main`, #53187 only keeps them while prompt metadata is pending), so `tokens` streams already drop a finish only chunk. #47933 (open) fixes that for `tokens` by emitting the terminal chunk when `finish_reason` is set. Phase 1 builds on it and also emits chunks that carry only new text.

#### 5. Logprobs

At `text` and `derender` levels, logprob entries carry decoded token strings and `bytes`, as `/derender` produces, instead of the `token_id:N` placeholders generate emits today. The tokens level shape follows #57574.

Dense logprobs are the expensive case. At `top_logprobs=20` the benchmark measured 355 µs per logprob-bearing token and 0.83 of a frontend core within 1.2× of the GPU's token rate. On a tokenizer loaded server that cost is already paid at the `tokens` level: `LogprobsProcessor` decodes every top-k token whenever `sampling_params.detokenize` is true and generate then discards the strings. Clients that want wide logprobs off the decode host send `output_mode="tokens"` with `detokenize: false` (which rules out `stop` strings) or use a `--tokens-only` pool. The Phase 1 docs should say so.

#### 6. Validation (fail loud)

- `output_mode != "tokens"` on a server without a tokenizer → **400**. Today's no-op detokenizer returns `""`, so a naive implementation would return empty text with a 200 for any request routed to a `--tokens-only` pool.
- `output_mode != "tokens"` with `sampling_params.detokenize` explicitly `false` → **400**.
- `chat_request` set without `output_mode="derender"` → **400**, rather than silently ignoring it.
- `output_mode="derender"` without `chat_request` on a server with a reasoning or tool parser configured → **400**, rather than falling back to plain text that may contain reasoning or tool call markup.

**Rollout note:** `GenerateRequest` is a plain pydantic `BaseModel`, so servers without this change ignore `output_mode` and return tokens only with a 200. Clients should check that `output_mode` in the response matches the request. Older servers don't return it.

#### 7. Role agnostic P/D usage

The field has no behavior tied to pod role or `kv_transfer_params`. The same decode pod may serve some requests decode only and others after a remote prefill, so role keyed behavior would differ across those paths. Orchestrators set `output_mode` and `chat_request` on the terminal leg only. If they reach a tokenizer free prefill pool anyway, the 400 above surfaces the misconfiguration.

For llm-d: the coordinator builds the prefill request from scratch, so it needs no change. The NIXL v2 sidecar reuses the client body for prefill and overrides a fixed set of fields (`stream`, token limits, `kv_transfer_params`). It would need to reset `output_mode` and drop `chat_request` on the prefill request, keeping both for decode. Resetting only `output_mode` leaves `chat_request` on a `tokens` request, which section 6 rejects.

#### 8. Decoupling `--tokens-only`

A decode pool needs the generate API surface *with* a tokenizer. `--tokens-only` currently does four jobs:

| Job | Where | Proposal |
|---|---|---|
| Skip tokenizer init | [arg_utils](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/engine/arg_utils.py#L2385-L2386) | keep |
| Force `detokenize=False` | [factories](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/factories.py#L61) → [serving](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py#L249-L250) | keep |
| Register `/abort_requests` | [api_router](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/api_router.py#L77) | also register when generate is served on a tokenizer loaded server (open question 4) |
| Imply scale-out endpoints | [factories](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/factories.py#L73) | keep |

A decode pool then runs `--enable-scale-out` with a tokenizer and without `--tokens-only`.

#### 9. Parity and shared code

The inline path and `/derender` must produce identical output or clients get different text depending on deployment.

- Both go through the same `Parser` code, with no parallel copy.
- Extend the round-trip parity test (#48617, streaming added in #57922) to assert `generate(output_mode=X)` matches `derender(generate(output_mode="tokens"))` for `text` and `derender`, batch and streaming.
- Streaming derender drops logprobs on `main`, so the streaming logprob checks depend on #55029.
- **Stop strings.** Inline levels follow the engine's stop handling, like `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`: a matched stop string is cut from the text unless `include_stop_str_in_output` is set. Token IDs keep every generated token, so decoding them in `/derender` brings the stop string back, plus anything after it in the same token. For requests with `stop`, the test asserts inline output matches the coupled endpoint and that `/derender` output starts with the inline text and differs only after it. The `tokens` leg has to run on a tokenizer-loaded server, since `--tokens-only` rejects `stop` with a 400 (#57058). `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat` re-decodes token IDs, so the Phase 2 inline path has to apply the stop truncation before parsing.
- **End of stream.** Tests cover a final chunk carrying only buffered text or only a `finish_reason`, including after `/abort_requests` (section 4).

#### 10. Rust frontend

The Rust frontend serves generate over HTTP and gRPC and both need the change. The protocol should be agreed here once and mirrored in both with the Rust frontend owners.

**HTTP.** `rust/src/server/src/routes/inference/generate/types.rs` mirrors `GenerateRequest` / `GenerateResponse`. It takes `output_mode`, `chat_request`, `text`, `message` and `delta` to also mirror the per level response types. For example, with a `#[serde(tag = "output_mode")]` enum that defaults to `tokens` when the tag is missing. The proto keeps optional fields. A proto `oneof` doesn't fit because every level carries `token_ids`.

**gRPC.** `rust/proto/inference.proto` (`Inference.Generate` / `GenerateStream`, enabled with `--grpc-port`) already serves most of the `text` level. It accepts `token_ids` and `kv_transfer_params` and returns decoded `text` on every `SequenceOutput` because `ResponseOptions.output_text` defaults to `true`. That's the reverse of HTTP generate where `tokens` is the default. gRPC shapes responses with per-field `ResponseOptions` flags rather than one mode, so the levels map onto flags:

| Level | gRPC today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | `output_text: false`, `output_token_ids: true` | none |
| `text` | `output_text: true` (default) | resolved logprob tokens |
| `derender` | not supported | `DerenderOptions` on `ResponseOptions`, `ParsedOutput` on `SequenceOutput` |

Proposed additions. All are new fields or messages, so they're wire compatible:

```proto
message ResponseOptions {
  ...
  // Set for the derender level. output_text stays independent.
  // Set it false to drop the raw text.
  optional DerenderOptions derender = 9;
}

message DerenderOptions {
  // Post-adjust_request ChatCompletionRequest (open question 2).
  google.protobuf.Struct chat_request = 1;
}

message SequenceOutput {
  ...
  // Set for the derender level. The full message in Generate, a delta in GenerateStream.
  optional ParsedOutput parsed = 11;
}

message ParsedOutput {
  optional string content = 1;
  optional string reasoning = 2;
  repeated ToolCall tool_calls = 3;
}

message ToolCall {
  uint32 index = 1;
  string id = 2;         // first delta for this index only when streaming
  string name = 3;       // first delta for this index only when streaming
  string arguments = 4;  // full JSON in Generate, a fragment in GenerateStream
}
```

- **Logprobs.** Sampled and candidate logprobs carry token IDs only. `CandidateTokenInfo.TokenInfo` already has `text = 4` and `token_bytes = 5` commented out. The `text` level fills them and adds the same for the sampled token, matching section 5.
- **Finish reason.** `FinishInfo.FinishReason` gains `TOOL_CALLS` for the `finish_reason` rewrite `/derender` does when tool calls were emitted.
- **Parser context.** `chat_request` travels as `google.protobuf.Struct`, the same way `kv_transfer_params` does, until open question 2 settles its shape.
- **Validation.** Section 6's 400s become `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The no-tokenizer case doesn't come up because the Rust frontend doesn't support `--tokens-only` or `--skip-tokenizer-init` yet and always loads a tokenizer.
- **Streaming.** `GenerateStream` stays server streaming. Parsing runs with the request, so the client has nothing to send after it and bidirectional streaming isn't needed (Alternatives, item 7). `GenerateStream` forwards every decoded event without filtering on new token IDs, so the end of stream gap in section 4 may not apply here. The section 9 tests should confirm it.
- **Parity.** The `derender` level on both Rust surfaces uses the Rust parsers in `rust/src/parser` and depends on the Rust `/derender` work, which has stalled: #53223 closed unmerged on 2026-09-17 and the draft follow-ups #53418 / #53419 haven't moved since 2026-09-10. The Rust `derender` level needs someone to pick that stack back up. The section 9 parity tests also run against the Rust frontend so Rust and Python produce the same output.
- **Release.** The proto change ships with a `vllm-proto` version bump in the same PR, checked by `cargo-semver-checks` (see `rust/proto/README.md`).
- **Out of scope.** `vllm serve --grpc` uses the external `smg-grpc-servicer` package with its own proto.

#### 11. Phasing

| Phase | Scope | PR(s)
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `output_mode` field, `text` level (batch and streaming), logprob resolution, validation, `/abort_requests` decoupling, docs, latency benchmarks (section 12) | #58588 |
| 2 | `derender` level, batch: `chat_request` context, `message` on the choice, reusing `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat` | |
| 3 | `derender` level, streaming: request-scoped parsers, `delta` on stream choices, parity CI extension, latency benchmarks (section 12) | |
| — | Rust frontend mirror, tracked with the Rust frontend owners | |

#### 12. Latency benchmarks

The CPU numbers above don't cover latency. The Phase 1 and Phase 3 PRs report TTFT and TPOT for:

- inline `text` / `derender` against generate plus streaming derender, across concurrency levels and response lengths.
- `tokens` requests on the same pod, with and without `text` or `derender` traffic mixed in.

#### Alternatives considered

1. **Streaming derender as-is (#47161).** Keeps the GPU tier tokenizer free but puts a round trip and echoed state on every chunk, plus replay for parsed output. It stays the right tool for stateless postprocessing (RL, batch, gateways that own postprocessing). This RFC complements it and doesn't replace it.
2. **The gateway composes generate + derender.** The per chunk hop moves from client to gateway rather than going away. Holding state in the gateway instead means reimplementing postprocessing there.
3. **Server-side derender sessions keyed by `request_id`.** Rejected in #47161 (Option B) over session lifecycle, eviction and memory. The derender tier has no live request to attach state to. The generate server does.
4. **Token IDs on `/v1/chat/completions`.** Chat has no token ID input (`messages` is required). Even with one, a render produced `GenerateRequest` carries resolved `SamplingParams` that don't map back onto OpenAI request fields
   without re-resolving and orchestrators on the generate format would have to run two wire formats.
5. **Run the coupled OpenAI server on decode pools.** Decode pods leave the generate protocol with the same
   two format problem as (4).
6. **Reuse `sampling_params.detokenize` as the switch.** It defaults to `True`, so every existing response on a
   tokenizer loaded server would grow text and token only clients would pay for detokenization by default.
7. **gRPC bidirectional streaming derender** (suggested by @andylolu2 on slack). The client opens one bidi stream to the derender tier, sends the parser context once, then forwards each generate chunk. The parser lives on the stream until it closes. That removes the echoed `stream_state`, the per chunk `chat_request` and replay. It also answers the lifecycle and eviction objections behind (3) because state lasts exactly as long as the stream. It doesn't remove the hop though. Every chunk still passes from the generate stream through the derender stream on the TPOT path and clients would need gRPC next to the HTTP generate format. If a derender replica fails mid stream, the parser state goes with it and the client has to reconnect and replay. A WebSocket would give the same stream lifetime on the HTTP stack. This complements the RFC rather than replacing it. It fits #57571 as an alternative to the parser cache for consumers that want a tokenizer free GPU tier.

#### Costs and risks

- **CPU on the decode host.** Detokenization and parsing run in the API server process, not the engine core. They don't block the scheduler but they use host CPU. `text` adds little on a tokenizer loaded server because detokenization already runs there today. Parsing and logprob resolution are the new work. In the benchmark, with the GPU saturated, the in-process frontend stayed under 0.25 of a core for chat, reasoning and tool-calling traffic (24–144 µs per token), at least 3.5× headroom over the GPU's token rate. That was one A100 and a faster GPU narrows the gap.
  `--api-server-count` scales the frontend if it becomes the limit. Dense logprobs are the exception (section 5). Opt-in per request bounds the cost to the traffic that asks for it.
- **Parser config drift.** Decode pools need the same `--reasoning-parser`, `--tool-call-parser` and `--enable-auto-tool-choice` as the render tier. That's the same obligation the derender tier already has.
- **Two call sites for postprocessing.** Mitigated by shared `Parser` code and the parity CI in section 9.
- **Security.** The inline path postprocesses engine produced tokens bounded by the request's resolved limits. It doesn't accept caller supplied output token IDs the way `/derender` does, so it doesn't need `/derender`'s explicit bounds checks. `chat_request` is caller supplied and needs the same validation as on the chat and derender endpoints.

#### Open questions

1. ~**Response shape.**~ RESOLVED. An extended generate format with `text` / `message` / `delta` (proposed) or return `ChatCompletionResponse` / `ChatCompletionStreamResponse` directly for `output_mode="derender"`? The latter is a drop-in for existing `/derender` consumers but the endpoint's response schema would then depend on a request field and the generate only fields would need a home. *Feedback so far:*
   - @nilig supports extending the generate response format (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5692634586).
   - @DarkLight1337 prefers separate response classes per `output_mode` for type checking (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5794326266).
2. **Parser context.** Embed the post-`adjust_request` `chat_request` (proposed), or have `/render` emit a slim derender context (`tools`, `tool_choice`, `chat_template_kwargs`, plus `adjust_request`-derived state) that clients pass through? The slim form is smaller but first needs a settled answer to the open `adjust_request` question from #42729. *Feedback so far:*
   - #42729 now proposes re-running `adjust_request` on the derender side. Once that's settled it answers this one too.
3. **Naming.** `output_mode` with `tokens | text | derender`, or something else?
4. **`/abort_requests`.** Register it whenever generate is served, add a separate flag or leave it tied to `--tokens-only`? *Feedback so far:*
   - @nilig wants it whenever generate is served, including on decode pools that load a tokenizer (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5692634586).
   - #55521 adds a general `/abort_requests` on every `vllm serve` server, where an empty or missing `request_ids` aborts all in-flight requests. The scale-out route returns 400 for a missing `request_ids`. If #55521 lands, the two routes clash on `--tokens-only` servers and the semantics need to be reconciled. That would also answer this question.
5. **Completions shaped parsing.** Is `text` enough for completions shaped clients or does anyone need reasoning/tool parsing on completions? Parsing on `/v1/completions/derender` is chat-only today. *Feedback so far:*
   - @shimib's logprob-heavy traffic is completions shaped and needs `text` plus resolved logprobs, not parsing (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033).
   - #42729 records that completions don't parse, which matches @shimib's feedback. #57922 documented it in `derenderer.md`.

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@chaunceyjiang @DarkLight1337 @vMaroon @NickLucche @nilig @njhill @robertgshaw2-redhat @sagearc @BugenZhao

### Any Other Things.

**Related work**
- #47161 / #50550: streaming derender and its parse path. Complementary to this RFC (Alternatives, item 1).
- #47313: adds `stop_reason` to generate response choices. It touches the same protocol and serving files, and the matched stop string would let `/derender` cut its text there too (section 9).
- #36983 / #51641: `delta_text` and `delta_token_ids` desync when stop strings are buffered. Streaming `text` inherits this and should use the fix.
- #53223 / #53418 / #53419: Rust `/derender` endpoints. #53223 closed unmerged and the drafts have stalled (section 10).
- #47933: emits the terminal `finish_reason` chunk on `tokens` streams, including after an abort (section 4).
- #55029: resolved logprobs on streaming derender chunks. The streaming logprob parity checks in section 9 need it.

**Related bug: #57052.** Stop strings break on the scale-out token path in two ways. On `--tokens-only` servers `stop` was silently ignored and generation ran to EOS or `max_tokens` with a 200. #57058 fixed that and the server now returns 400. On the derender side the stop text leaks back into the output because `/derender` re-decodes every token ID (section 9). That part is still open. Once decode pools run with a tokenizer, `stop` works there too.

**Out of scope**
- Skipping detokenization for `output_mode="tokens"` on tokenizer loaded servers where today it runs and its output is discarded. It's a worthwhile performance follow up but it changes existing behavior (`stop` strings need detok).
- Any change to `/derender` itself.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Performance]: GDN hybrid (Qwen3.8-27B, fp8 KV, TP2): c32 aggregate throughput steps -24% when the profiled KV pool is below ~190k tokens (<=116 blocks); c8 and single-stream unaffected
body:
### Summary

On a GDN hybrid (Qwen3.8-27B, INT4 weights, fp8 KV, TP=2) the aggregate throughput of 32 concurrent short requests drops by ~24 % when the profiled GPU KV pool is **below ~190k tokens (≤116 unified blocks)**, and is fully recovered when the pool is **≥ ~190k tokens (≥121 blocks)**. Each request needs only one block, `c8` and single-stream numbers are identical in every configuration, and the pool size is the only variable that tracks the step. Because the memory profiler lands the *same* launch at 183,028 or 191,884 tokens on different starts (~5 % variance), the c32 throughput of one production launch is a per-start coin flip.

Is there a per-step cap in the hybrid (Mamba/GDN state) scheduling path that is derived from the number of KV blocks, independent of `--max-num-seqs`? If this is expected, what is the right knob?

### Environment

- vLLM 0.28.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer attention backend, driver 616.56, WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33), 2× RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB
- Model: `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4`
- Launch (production): `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-cache-mode align --max-model-len 163840 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 3135 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` (block size 1568 = the unified hybrid block); one series with the LMCache MP connector, one without — the step is the same either way.

### Measurement

Probe: 512-token prompt → 256 output tokens; W1 single stream (3 reps), then c1 / c8 / c32 fired at once; aggregate tok/s over the batch wall.

| arm | max_len | util | connector | pool (tokens) | c32 agg t/s | c32 TTFT p95 | c8 agg | W1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 65,536 | 0.90 | yes | 169,301 | 230.4 | 26.4 s | 160.9 | 29.3 |
| B | 106,496 | 0.90 | yes | 178,452 | 230.6 | 26.4 s | 160.7 | 29.2 |
| C | 131,072 | 0.90 | yes | 180,588 | 229.3 | 26.6 s | 161.5 | 29.5 |
| D | 131,072 | 0.90 | no | 180,588 | 232.8 | 26.1 s | 162.4 | 29.7 |
| E | 163,840 | 0.90 | no | 183,028 | 232.0 | 26.3 s | 162.3 | 29.7 |
| F | 163,840 | 0.88 | yes | 172,696 | 229.6 | 26.4 s | 161.0 | 29.0 |
| **G** | 163,840 | 0.90 | yes | **191,884** | **300.6 / 302.7** | 11.3 s | 160.9 | 29.0 |
| G, batched 1568 | 163,840 | 0.90 | yes | 191,884 | 301.4 | 11.3 s | 160.4 | 29.2 |
| G, batched 4703 | 163,840 | 0.90 | yes | 191,884 | 301.2 | 11.2 s | 160.7 | 29.2 |
| G, `--max-num-seqs 40` | 163,840 | 0.90 | yes | 187,456 | 232.4 | 11.0 s | 161.7 | 29.4 |

- F vs G is the cleanest control: identical launch except util 0.88 → 0.90, i.e. the pool 172,696 → 191,884; c32 goes 230 → 301.
- In the slow arms c32 TTFT p95 is one full 256-token round (26 s) with per-request tok/s unchanged (9.8 vs 9.5), which looks like ~24 of the 32 streams are admitted and 8 wait for a slot.
- `--max-num-seqs 40` at a 187,456 pool admits all 32 (TTFT p95 11 s) but the aggregate stays at 232 — so the cap may be a per-step batch limit rather than admission.
- Ruled out: `--max-num-batched-tokens` (1568 / 3135 / 4703: no change), the connector's per-step cost (slow without it too), host state (re-runs reproduce), GPU clocks (P0, 2.5 GHz throughout).

### Question

1. Is there a per-step limit in the hybrid scheduling path that is derived from the number of KV blocks (rather than from `--max-num-seqs` / `--max-num-batched-tokens`)? The 116 → 121 block edge is very sharp for a workload where each request holds one block.
2. Is pinning the pool with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` (sized to the fast side) the recommended way to make this deterministic, or is there a scheduler knob for it? Pinning gives us the 190,408-token pool on every start, but skips the profile run, so we would rather not rely on it for production if there is a better handle.

### Repro

- Same launch, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.88` vs `0.90`, then 32 concurrent 512→256 requests; the aggregate steps by ~24 %.
- Probe: a small asyncio loop over `/v1/completions` (512-token prompt, `max_tokens=256`, 32 requests fired together, aggregate = total generated tokens / batch wall). Happy to attach it or run further arms on request.

title: [Bug]: MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm Lamport workspace silently disabled on cuda-bindings 13.4 — cudaIpcMemHandle_t.reserved removed
body:
## Summary

`LamportWorkspace` reads and writes `cudaIpcMemHandle_t.reserved`, which NVIDIA removed in `cuda-bindings` 13.4. The MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm path is silently disabled as a result:

```
AttributeError: 'cuda.bindings.runtime.cudaIpcMemHandle_t' object has no attribute 'reserved'
```

## Root cause

`reserved` is gone from both `cudaIpcMemHandle_t` and its parent `cudaIpcMemHandle_st`. From `cuda/bindings/runtime.pxd` in the published wheels:

```
13.0.3                        13.4.3
──────                        ──────
CUDA IPC memory handle        CUDA IPC memory handle
Attributes                    Methods
----------                    -------
reserved : bytes              getPtr()
Methods
-------
getPtr()
```

`vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/lamport_workspace.py` uses it twice — once to serialize the local handle for `all_gather_object`, once to rehydrate a peer's handle for `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle`:

```python
87:  all_handles, bytes(local_handle.reserved), group=process_group
95:  handle.reserved = all_handles[r]
```

## Impact

The call site in `rms_norm_tp.py:319-333` wraps this in a `try/except` intended for GPUs without P2P, so it degrades rather than crashes:

```
WARNING [rms_norm_tp.py:327] Failed to initialize MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm
Lamport workspace: ... Falling back to the eager allreduce + RMSNorm path.
```

On a `cuda-bindings` 13.4 environment this makes the fused kernel **unreachable**, and the fallback is silent — a perf regression with no error surfaced to the user. The only reason it is visible at all is `test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk`, which asserts the fused path is taken.

## Reproduction

`kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk` on `:nvidia: (H100) MiniMax Reduce RMS Kernels`. Deterministic across dtypes, and the split tracks `cuda-bindings` exactly:

| Lane | `cuda-bindings` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| torch nightly [90640](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90640) (09-23) | 13.4.3 | **fails** |
| torch nightly [90830](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90830) (09-24) | 13.4.3 | **fails**, identical signature |
| `main` nightly [90897](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90897) | 13.0.3 | passes |
| torch 2.14.0 RC [90968](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90968) | 13.0.3 (pinned) | passes, 96 passed / 13 skipped, no warning |

Two independent nightly builds fail with byte-identical output; both CUDA 13.0 lanes pass. This is not flaky and not torch-version-specific — it follows the `cuda-bindings` version.

## Questions

1. What is the supported way to serialize/deserialize a `cudaIpcMemHandle_t` on `cuda-bindings` >= 13.4? `getPtr()` is the only documented member left, but I have not confirmed the intended round-trip for shipping a handle through `all_gather_object`. A fix likely needs a version guard, since CUDA 12 / 13.0 images still have `.reserved`.

2. Possibly separate: `requirements/test/cuda.txt` pins `cuda-bindings==13.0.3`, yet the torch-nightly lane resolves 13.4.3 despite a CUDA 13.0.2 base image. I did not chase down what overrides the pin there, but if the constraint is meant to hold on that lane, it is not holding.

Happy to put up a PR for (1) given a steer on the replacement API.

title: [RFC]: Publish Mooncake Store residency once per complete block
body:
### Motivation

`MooncakeStoreConnector` publishes Store residency on the same KV event stream as the engine's local prefix cache: one `BlockStored` per block, per rank, currently with `medium="cpu"`. Three things about that stream are wrong or undefined, and they share a cause: the fact being published — the pool holds this block — belongs to the pool, but each rank constructs it on its own and the engine merges the copies by counting events.

1. **A block is announced only if the path that wrote it remembers to.** `store_mask` keeps mamba/SSM groups out of the positional save, so their `align` boundary states are written by the hand-off path, which published nothing. A consumer intersecting the cache groups of a block therefore scored every mamba block a miss on the rank that had just stored it. #58293 fixes this (one write path that announces what it committed, plus the group's `kv_cache_spec_kind`), and adds the missing diagnostics for hand-offs that are never persisted.
2. **The same block can be announced twice.** The cross-worker merge counts only the workers that reported in that engine step (`increment_workers` per contributing worker in `kv_connector/utils.py`), so when two ranks finish the same block in different steps, each announcement satisfies the quorum by itself.
3. **Nothing retracts a block.** The connector emits no `BlockRemoved`, and `reset_cache`, which issues `remove_all` on the master, emits no `AllBlocksCleared`, so a consumer's view of the Store only grows. `medium` is a literal, so an object the Store placed on disk is still reported as CPU; the mapping from the written replica tier to the event's wire value is undefined.

#### How to reproduce

Start a `mooncake_master`, point `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` at it, and serve a hybrid model:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen3.5-4B --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' \
  --kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events":true,"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://*:5557","replay_endpoint":"tcp://*:5558","topic":"kv-events"}'
```

Send three distinct ~4.4k-token prompts, then repeat the first. Compare:

- the objects the master lists (`GET /get_all_keys` on the master's metrics port), grouped by the `@group:N@` tag of each key;
- the events received on `tcp://127.0.0.1:5558` (a DEALER that sends `(b"", start_sequence_as_8_bytes)`; a plain SUB subscriber drops the first batches), grouped by `group_idx`.

On the base commit the Store holds 33 blocks (groups 0/1/2 are the GDN state groups with 3 each, group 3 is full attention with 24) and 24 are announced; the missing 9 are exactly the mamba groups. The same run shows 8 of the 24 group-3 blocks announced twice with identical payloads, and `kv_cache_spec_kind` absent on every Store-side event.

In one observed run with #58293, all 33 blocks were announced once, with `mamba` / `full_attention` set. This validates the missing-write-path fix in item 1 for that run; it does not establish the lifetime, cross-rank once-only semantics in item 2. #58293 does not change the cross-worker event aggregation or its quorum rule, so duplicate behavior can still depend on rank timing. A repeat run is required to evaluate item 2 independently.

### Proposed Change

1. **Define the event.** A `BlockStored` from this connector means "the Store holds a complete copy of this block for this cache group, on medium M". Complete means every rank namespace `lookup` probes for that group has committed its objects — the same set that decides whether a later request can hit the block.
2. **Publish it once.** Build the scheduler-side accumulator with the number of workers in the engine and keep it for the connector's lifetime, instead of adopting the container of whichever step contributed first. An event then waits until the required coverage is reached and is released exactly once. The quorum rule should be stated over `lookup_key_prefixes` rather than over worker counts, so PCP/PP layouts are covered by construction. This is a follow-up to #58293, which only fixes the missing write-path announcement.
3. **Report the tier that was written.** Derive the event medium from the replica that accepted the write: use `CPU` for a memory-backed replica, `STORAGE` for a disk-backed replica, and `None` when the tier is unavailable or unknown. Do not emit a hard-coded lowercase `cpu` value.
4. **Retract what the connector itself invalidates.** After `reset_cache` has drained pending Store work and `remove_all` succeeds on the master, emit `AllBlocksCleared`. If the reset fails, do not emit a clear event; consumers must retain their last known Store view. Evictions stay with the pool, which the connector cannot observe.
5. Keep the connector as the only publisher on the vLLM event stream, so a router serving vLLM does not also have to consume the Store's own key-level channel.

### Feedback Period

One week.

### Any Other Things

- #58293 is the completeness fix this builds on; it intentionally does not implement the lifetime quorum, tier reporting, or reset retraction in items 2–4. Those items can land as independent follow-up PRs.
- #52731 covers the load path reporting the tier it read from, which is the read-side half of item 3.
- The offloading connector settled the same ownership question by letting the tier-owned tracker publish; its `BlockStored` metadata is the schema this connector's events are converging on (#51243, #51614, #54325), and #49413 refactors that connector's event path.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash: CUDA illegal memory access in FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA backend under TP+EP and MTP decoding on H20 (vLLM nightly 260904)
body:
### Your current environment

- **GPUs**: 8x NVIDIA H20 (SM90)
- **vLLM**: nightly image `vllm-nightly-260904`
  - Custom image: `mirrors.tencent.com/abo/nvidia-serve:vllm-nightly-260904`
  - Base image: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f5df5cc3302b5f404848c4eca88d7bf7ed5226e151c056da22816d7734644d67`
  - Upstream commit: `8a728663c1c3eeace834a95f5654fa653cc1998c` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8a728663c1c3eeace834a95f5654fa653cc1998c)
- **Python**: 3.12.3
- **PyTorch**: 2.13.0+cu130
- **CUDA**: Toolkit 13.0.2, Runtime 13.0.96-1
- **Model**: GLM-5.3-Flash 

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

Serving **GLM-5.3-Flash** on **8x NVIDIA H20** with vLLM nightly (`260904`). One engine worker (`Worker_TP2_EP2`) aborted with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` while building attention metadata inside the **FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA** backend (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`, called from `mamba_hybrid.py prepare_attn`). The fault is reported at a host-side sync point (`positions[:num_rows].cpu()`), so the actual faulting kernel is likely earlier in the async stream, not necessarily the FlashInfer path itself.

### Serving config (EXTRA_PARAMS)

```
--enable-expert-parallel
--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
--tool-call-parser glm47
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--reasoning-parser glm45
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
```

Load: input/output length 65536, batch_size 32 (crash observed mid-serving on a normal chat completion request).


### Expected behavior

No illegal memory access; engine keeps serving under TP+EP + MTP speculative decoding.

### Questions / info we can still provide

Happy to run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, and to bisect with EP off / MTP off / prefix-caching off, and to report actual attention block size + kpool indexer page size. Please tell us what diagnostics would help most.

### Related issues checked (not duplicates)

- **#55221** – same backend file (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`) on CUDA TP2, but different symptom (fp8 KV dtype rejected by `plan()` + indexer prefill workspace sizing), no runtime illegal memory access.
- **#55280** – GLM-5.3-Flash hybrid `block_size=1152` -> 32-entry paged-MQA GPU memory fault on MTP decode, but ROCm/gfx942 only; no CUDA reproduction reported. Possibly the same family of hybrid KV-geometry issue; we are checking our `block_size` / `index_kpool` geometry.
- **#53142** – hybrid Mamba align precopy illegal memory access on prefix-cache resume (`mamba-cache-mode=align`): demonstrates that an async CUDA fault can surface later inside an attention backend. We have not confirmed whether our deployment uses `--enable-prefix-caching` / align mode.
- **#55279** – deterministic CUDA IMA in DFlash2 spec decode; different decode method and GPU.

title: Idefics3/SmolVLM: num_patches=0 for non-tiled images mis-sizes pixel_values while the prompt still reserves image_seq_len placeholder tokens
body:
### Description

For Idefics3/SmolVLM, when an image doesn't get tiled (`do_image_splitting=False`, or splitting enabled but the image is already small enough that no split is needed), `Idefics3ProcessingInfo` computes `num_patches=0` for that image and uses it to size the image's `pixel_values`/`pixel_attention_mask` slice in the multimodal field config, while the prompt still correctly reserves `image_seq_len` placeholder tokens for it. The zero-size slice doesn't match the real, non-empty pixel data HF's own preprocessing produces for that image, which should surface as a `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` token-count mismatch (0 actual vs `image_seq_len` expected) at inference time.

### Where the numbers diverge

`get_number_of_image_patches` in HF's `Idefics3ImageProcessor` (checked directly against `transformers==5.5.3`, the minimum vLLM currently requires per `requirements/common.txt`):

```python
# transformers/models/idefics3/image_processing_idefics3.py, v5.5.3
def get_number_of_image_patches(self, height, width, images_kwargs):
    ...
    num_patches = num_rows = num_cols = 0
    if do_image_splitting:
        ...
        if resized_height > max_height or resized_width > max_width:
            num_rows = math.ceil(resized_height / max_height)
            num_cols = math.ceil(resized_width / max_width)
            num_patches = num_rows * num_cols + 1
    return num_patches, num_rows, num_cols
```

`num_patches` stays `0` whenever `do_image_splitting=False`, or whenever splitting is enabled but the image doesn't actually exceed `max_image_size`. This is consistent with the real preprocessing path, `split_images()` in the same class, which returns `num_splits_h = num_splits_w = 0` in exactly the same "no split needed" case, but still returns `frames = [image]`, one real frame, the global image itself.

`vllm/model_executor/models/idefics3.py` uses this `num_patches` value in two places that end up disagreeing with each other:

1. `Idefics3MultiModalProcessor._call_hf_processor` (line ~331-340):
   ```python
   num_patches = [
       self.info.get_num_patches(image_width=size.width, image_height=size.height,
                                  processor=hf_processor, mm_kwargs=mm_kwargs)
       for size in image_sizes
   ]
   processed_outputs["num_patches"] = torch.tensor(num_patches)
   ```
   This directly reuses HF's `num_patches` (0 in the no-split case) as `size_per_item` for `MultiModalFieldConfig.flat_from_sizes("image", num_patches)` in `_get_mm_fields_config` (line ~356-359), which slices the flattened `pixel_values`/`pixel_attention_mask` tensor per image using exactly these sizes. A `0` here means vLLM will slice a zero-row chunk for that image, even though HF's actual preprocessing produced one real frame of pixel data for it.

2. `Idefics3ProcessingInfo.get_image_repl` (line ~204-247) builds the prompt text for the same image independently, and has its own explicit special case for this:
   ```python
   _, grid_h, grid_w = self._get_image_feature_grid_size(...)
   if grid_w == 0 and grid_h == 0:
       return global_img_placeholder + fake_image_token   # image_seq_len <image> tokens
   ```
   So the prompt correctly ends up with `image_seq_len` placeholder tokens for this image, that part is right, it's specifically the `pixel_values` sizing in (1) that doesn't have an equivalent special case.

### Why this should be user-visible

`MultiModalFieldConfig.flat_from_sizes` slices a flattened tensor using `size_per_item` as consecutive chunk sizes (`vllm/multimodal/inputs.py`, `flat_from_sizes`). A `0` entry for an image whose actual pixel data isn't empty means either that image's real pixel rows get silently reattributed to a neighboring image's slice in the same batch (in a multi-image request mixing split and non-split images), or, in the single-image case, the vision tower ends up running on a 0-row input and producing 0 embeddings for that image. Either way, `is_multimodal.sum()` (from the correctly-sized prompt, `image_seq_len` positions) won't match `len(mm_embeds_flat)` (0, or misattributed from another image) when `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` runs (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py`, ~line 545-550), which is exactly the shape-mismatch `RuntimeError` that function's `except` branch is written to catch and report.

### Reproduction

Any Idefics3/SmolVLM checkpoint with `do_image_splitting=False` set (either via `--mm-processor-kwargs '{"do_image_splitting": false}'`, or a `preprocessor_config.json` that sets that default), or any image small enough that splitting doesn't trigger even with the default `do_image_splitting=True`, should hit this on the very first request containing that image. `smolvlm.py` inherits this class unmodified, so it's affected the same way.

### Notes

`tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_smolvlm.py` doesn't appear to cover the no-split path (this is inferred from the file layout in the repo, I didn't run the suite), which is consistent with this not having been caught yet, dummy/test images there are sized to force splitting.

Happy to help narrow down the exact runtime error text if useful, wanted to get the root-cause diff (the `num_patches=0`-but-real-pixel-data-exists mismatch, specifically in the `_get_mm_fields_config` sizing, not the prompt string which is already correct) written up precisely first.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Describe the bug The non-streaming `/v1/messages` response has no `stop_sequence` key unless generation stopped on a matched stop string. `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py` serializes the response with `generator.model_dump(exclude_none=True)`, and `AnthropicMessagesResponse` declares `stop_sequence: str | None = None`, so the null value is dropped from the wire. `stop_reason` is dropped the same way when it is null. Anthropic's published schema lists both as required, nullable members of `Message` (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages, response fields `stop_reason` and `stop_sequence`; in the OpenAPI spec the SDKs are generated from, `Message.required` lists both and `stop_sequence` is `string | null`). Anthropic's own non-streaming examples carry `"stop_sequence": null`. The official SDKs tolerate the missing key; a schema-validating proxy does not, which is how this was found (vLLM Semantic Router, vllm-project/semantic-router#3500). This is the non-streaming twin of #55324. That one was `exclude_unset=True` on the streaming `message_delta`; this one is `exclude_none=True` on the buffered response, so the streaming fix does not cover it. `message_start` on the stream already carries both keys explicitly. No `stop_sequence`. Same on main at `828f4f19` (2026-09-10): `api_router.py` line 82. ### To Reproduce No GPU needed. Build the route's FastAPI app with a mocked handler that returns an `AnthropicMessagesResponse(stop_reason="end_turn")`, POST `/v1/messages` with `"stream": false`, and inspect `response.json()`: `"stop_sequence"` is not a key. Inspecting the model attribute hides the omission (`stop_sequence is None`); `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` reproduces it. With a server: ``` curl -s http://:8000/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: x' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -d '{"model":"","max_tokens":16,"stream":false,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: OK"}]}' ``` ### Expected behavior `"stop_sequence": null` (and `"stop_reason": null` if ever null) on the non-streaming response, matching the schema and the streaming `message_delta` after #55325. What `exclude_none` prunes today should stay pruned: the vLLM extension fields (`kv_transfer_params`, `ec_transfer_params`) and the members of each content block that do not apply to its type. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: MFU/MBU bills linear-attention layers of hybrid models as full attention; reported bandwidth exceeds the GPU's peak
body:
### Your current environment

RTX 4090 24 GB (spec 1,008 GB/s; memory clock 10,501 MHz per `nvidia-smi -q`), driver 590.48.01 (CUDA 13.1), Ubuntu 24.04, vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev80+g26f49e336` (nightly cu130 wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.17.0. The rented machine is gone, so I do not have `collect_env.py` output; `vllm/v1/metrics/` is unchanged between `26f49e336` and current `main` (`8b84e150`, 2026-09-24).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`AttentionMetrics` bills full attention (QKV/O weights, KV-cache reads, attention FLOPs) for every one of `num_hidden_layers`. Hybrid models with linear-attention layers only have full attention in a fraction of them: Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next use 3 Gated DeltaNet layers for every full-attention layer (`layer_types`, `full_attention_interval: 4`). #55624 handles sliding-window/full alternation but not linear-attention or Mamba layers, so the reported MBU for these models is not physically possible.

Config-only check (no GPU):

```python
from tests.v1.metrics.test_perf_metrics import create_mock_vllm_config
from vllm.transformers_utils.config import get_config
from vllm.v1.metrics.perf import ModelMetrics

mm = ModelMetrics(create_mock_vllm_config(get_config("Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", trust_remote_code=False)))
print({m.component_type(): getattr(m, "num_hidden_layers", None) for m in mm.metrics})
# {'attn': 32, 'ffn': 32, 'unembed': None}; layer_types has 8 "full_attention" and 24 "linear_attention"
```

Measured with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-mfu-metrics` (`VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=2`) and `vllm bench serve` (random prompts, 512 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, 3 × batch requests per cell). The table only uses 2-second log intervals inside the benchmark's wall time that have no prefill in them (`Avg prompt throughput: 0.0`), so it is pure decode:

| batch × context | reported GB/s, median (run 1 / run 2) | intervals above 1,008 GB/s | same cells, layer count corrected (see below) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 × 8k | 1,164 / 1,165 | 8/8, 8/8 | 602, 0/9 above |
| 8 × 16k | 1,538 / 1,536 | 10/10, 11/11 | 652, 0/11 above |
| 32 × 8k | 1,821 / 1,831 | 10/10, 10/10 | 645, 0/13 above |

- A device-to-device copy on the same card reaches 918 GB/s (read + write, 3 trials), so the reported numbers are not physically possible.
- Control: Qwen3-4B (dense, same size, same script, same machine) never exceeds the peak: 0 of 32 decode intervals, max 881 GB/s.
- Intervention: counting only the 8 full-attention layers (a small parser reading `layer_types` / `layers_block_type`) removes every over-peak interval on the same cells.

The corrected column is not the right answer either. Dropping the 24 linear-attention layers from attention without billing them as anything leaves out their weights (1,011 M parameters for Qwen3.5-4B, counted from the safetensors headers) and their recurrent state, so the estimate becomes about 0.75× of the bytes actually moved. A correct fix needs a linear-attention component: weights, the per-request recurrent and conv state read and written every step, and nothing that grows with context. Hand accounting of what the model actually reads shows the current code over-bills bytes per decode step by about 1.43× at 8 × 8k and about 2× at 32 × 8k, and under-bills slightly at 1 × 1k.

A smaller related gap: the Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next attention has an output gate (`attn_output_gate: true`; `q_proj` is `[8192, 2560]`, twice the query width), which `qkv_weight` / `qkv_proj` do not include.

Limits of this report: one GPU and one hybrid model measured; Qwen3-Next, Jamba, Falcon-H1 only checked at config level. `ncu` DRAM counters were not available in the container, so "bytes actually moved" comes from the parameter and state accounting above, not a hardware counter.

Not a duplicate as far as I can tell: no open or closed issue or PR covers MFU/MBU for linear-attention or Mamba layers (searched 2026-09-25). The two open PRs touching `perf.py` (#55474, #54228) do not touch layer counting.

I'd like to work on the fix (linear-attention component plus layer-type parsing, with tests) if that direction sounds right to the maintainers of this area.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the scripts, drive the measurements on my rented GPU and draft this report. I reviewed the logs and the results.

title: [Bug]: `VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS=1` shuts the server down on the first request (msgspec `ValidationError` on `context_breakdown`)
body:
### Your current environment

RTX 4090 24 GB, driver 590.48.01 (CUDA 13.1), Ubuntu 24.04, vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev80+g26f49e336` (nightly cu130 wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.17.0. The rented machine is gone, so I do not have `collect_env.py` output; the relevant code (`vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py`, `vllm/v1/serial_utils.py`, `vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py`) is unchanged between `26f49e336` and current `main` (`8b84e150`, 2026-09-24), and the field that triggers the bug is in `v0.30.0`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--enable-mfu-metrics` and `VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS=1`, the first request returns HTTP 500 and the API server shuts down:

```text
msgspec.ValidationError: Expected `int`, got `array` - at `$[2].perf_stats.debug_stats.context_breakdown[...]`
```

Repro:

```bash
VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-mfu-metrics --max-model-len 20480
curl localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":32}'
# -> 500, server exits. Same command with VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS=0 -> 200.
```

Cause: `ModelMetrics.get_step_perf_stats_per_gpu` passes `asdict(ctx)` as `DebugPerfStats.context_breakdown`, which is typed `dict[str, int]`. #55624 added `ExecutionContext.requests: list[tuple[int, int, bool]]`, so `asdict(ctx)` now contains a list. The engine core encodes it fine, but the frontend decodes `EngineCoreOutputs` with `MsgpackDecoder(EngineCoreOutputs)` (type-checked), rejects it, and the output handler dies.

Minimal repro without a GPU:

```python
from dataclasses import asdict
from vllm.v1.metrics.perf import DebugPerfStats, ExecutionContext, PerfStats
from vllm.v1.serial_utils import MsgpackDecoder, MsgpackEncoder

ctx = ExecutionContext()
ctx.add(1024, 1024, is_prefill=True)
stats = PerfStats(1, 2, 3, DebugPerfStats(0.0, 1, 0, asdict(ctx), {}, {}, {}))
MsgpackDecoder(PerfStats).decode(MsgpackEncoder().encode(stats))
# msgspec.ValidationError: Expected `int`, got `array` - at `$.debug_stats.context_breakdown[...]`
```

What I checked on the 4090:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| server, `VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS=1`, 3 separate starts | 500 on every request, server down every time |
| server, `VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS=0` | 200, 200, server up |
| unit round trip above, 3 runs | 3/3 `ValidationError` |
| dropping the `requests` key from `context_breakdown` | unit 3/3 OK; server 3/3 OK (two curl runs and one MTP benchmark run with debug on) |

I have a one-line fix with a regression test (msgpack round trip through `EngineCoreOutputs`, the same path the server uses; it fails on `main` with the exact error above and passes with the fix) and will open a PR referencing this issue.

Not a duplicate as far as I can tell: no open or closed issue mentions `VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS`, `context_breakdown` or `DebugPerfStats` (searched 2026-09-25), and the two open PRs touching `perf.py` (#55474, #54228) do not change this code.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the repro scripts, drive the measurements on my rented GPU and draft this report. I reviewed the logs and the results.

### 🐛 Describe the bug With `method: ngram_gpu` + xgrammar structured outputs + `--async-scheduling`, the target model **verifies and accepts draft tokens that the grammar forbids**. The authoritative FSM then rejects them at commit time and the request is terminated: ``` ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-... for tokens 2585. Please file an issue. ERROR [scheduler.py:1654] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [2585] for request chatcmpl-... Terminating request. ERROR [serving.py:173] Request chatcmpl-... failed with an internal error during generation ``` Observable behavior is strongly **concurrency-dependent** (single in-flight request is clean; the async pipeline never overlaps): | symptom | measurement | |---|---| | `/v1/chat/completions` (grammar + penalties) | **~88% HTTP 500** at concurrency 4 (bf16: 178/200; NVFP4: 87/100) | | `/v1/completions` (token-id prompts, grammar) | zero HTTP errors but **silent truncation growing with load**: mean response chars 264 → 174 → 95 → 47 → 24 → 24 at concurrency 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 12 → 16; server-side mean generation length collapses ~70 → ~17.5 tokens/request | | concurrency 1 | outputs intact (~264 chars, normal lengths) | | drafting itself | healthy: ~67% acceptance, ≈1.9 accepted tokens/step — the speedup potential is real, which is what makes the silent-truncation mode dangerous | ## Root-cause analysis (v0.25.1 source) Under async scheduling the engine core and the model runner end up holding **two divergent views of the draft tokens** for a structured-output request: 1. In the deferred-output path, `Scheduler.update_draft_token_ids_in_output` (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`) validates drafts against the grammar (`grammar.validate_tokens`) and **patches invalid ones to `-1`** in `scheduler_output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens`, recording the count in `num_invalid_spec_tokens`. 2. The bitmask builder (`StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask`, `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`) treats a `-1` draft as "skip": it emits an **unconstrained bitmask row** for that position and sets `apply_bitmask = False` for the remainder of the window. 3. However, when ngram_gpu is used, the model runner **snapshots the *unpatched* dict** before the engine core patches it — `gpu_model_runner.py` (~line 4086): ```python # If ngram_gpu is used, we need to copy the scheduler_output to avoid # the modification has influence on the scheduler_output in engine core process. ``` so verification runs against the **original raw draft tokens**, not the grammar-filtered ones the bitmask was built for. 4. Nothing closes the gap: `num_invalid_spec_tokens` is consumed **only** by `make_spec_decoding_stats` — neither `gpu_model_runner.py` nor `rejection_sampler.py` reference it, so grammar-invalid draft positions are **never force-rejected**. Net effect: a grammar-illegal draft token is verified at an unconstrained position, accepted by the target model (it is perfectly plausible *text*), and then rejected by the authoritative FSM in `Scheduler.update_from_output` → `FINISHED_ERROR` (chat) or truncated output (token-id path). A second, compounding async-only mechanism: the 2-deep pipeline races draft validation against FSM advancement (drafts can be validated against an FSM that has not yet consumed the in-flight step's accepted tokens), which matches the observed concurrency-dependence. This half looks adjacent to PR #44993 (merged 2026-07-23, not yet in any release) — but #44993 is framed around reasoning parsers, and v0.25.1 already contains #44297 (the bonus-row fix for #44006), so what we hit appears to be an **unfixed residual specific to the ngram_gpu snapshot path**. ## Reproduction 1. Serve any model with the flags above (any nontrivial EBNF/JSON-schema grammar via xgrammar; large prompts are not required, but a grammar whose legal-token set is sparse makes it trigger faster). 2. Send ≥4 concurrent `/v1/chat/completions` requests with `structured_outputs.grammar` set and sampling enabled. 3. Watch for `Failed to advance FSM` / `grammar rejected tokens` in the engine log; HTTP 500s on chat requests; or compare output lengths at concurrency 1 vs 8 on `/v1/completions` (silent truncation). At concurrency 1 everything is clean, so smoke tests will not catch it. ## Workarounds verified - `{"method": "ngram", ...}` (CPU drafter) **with `--async-scheduling` removed** is fully correct in our testing (100/100 requests OK, no truncation, ~65% acceptance, and a −31% mean e2e latency win at our production operating point). Note plain `ngram` + `--async-scheduling` is already rejected at startup ("async scheduling is only supported with EAGLE/MTP/Draft Model/NGram GPU/DSpark"), which is what pushes users onto the broken `ngram_gpu` path in the first place. - Disabling speculative decoding obviously also avoids it. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Async MTP align mode reads accepted counts from mutable InputBatch rows
body:
### Your current environment

Source audit against the current vLLM `main` HEAD:

```text
commit: 83ad767eed3be3ee7f2df63be693bfaca5c7c922
checked: 2026-08-09
```

A native CUDA runtime reproduction has not yet been run against this commit. The runtime evidence below is from the equivalent vLLM-Ascend path; the latest upstream code-path finding is static and deterministic.

### Describe the bug

With all of the following enabled:

- async scheduling;
- MTP/speculative decoding;
- a hybrid Mamba/GDN model;
- `mamba_cache_mode="align"` (the default for hybrid models when prefix caching is enabled);

accepted-token counts produced by model iteration N are asynchronously copied into `InputBatch.num_accepted_tokens_cpu_tensor`. Before iteration N+1 consumes those counts, `_update_states()` removes/adds requests and runs `InputBatch.condense()`, mutating the same persistent row-indexed storage. `_prepare_inputs()` then synchronizes the copy and gathers previous-iteration counts through `prev_positions`, but it gathers them from the already-mutable `InputBatch` array.

Synchronization guarantees D2H completion; it does not preserve iteration-N request ownership for those rows. A wrong accepted count changes the Mamba/GDN state-copy offset and can produce repeated, dropped, or garbled tokens.

### Current `main` code path

1. The align postprocess passes the mutable InputBatch CPU tensor as the D2H destination:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83ad767eed3be3ee7f2df63be693bfaca5c7c922/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L1629-L1648

2. `postprocess_mamba_align_gpu()` performs a non-blocking copy into that tensor:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83ad767eed3be3ee7f2df63be693bfaca5c7c922/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py#L1190-L1243

3. On the next execution, `_update_states()` runs before `_prepare_inputs()`:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83ad767eed3be3ee7f2df63be693bfaca5c7c922/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L4292-L4343

4. `_update_states()` adds requests and condenses the persistent batch:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83ad767eed3be3ee7f2df63be693bfaca5c7c922/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L1550-L1561

5. New requests initialize their reused row to accepted count `1`, and `condense()` rewrites current per-row state:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83ad767eed3be3ee7f2df63be693bfaca5c7c922/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L485-L486
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83ad767eed3be3ee7f2df63be693bfaca5c7c922/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L708-L817

6. Only after those mutations, `_prepare_inputs()` synchronizes and gathers old row positions from the mutable InputBatch:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83ad767eed3be3ee7f2df63be693bfaca5c7c922/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L2148-L2170

### Concrete example

Iteration N produced:

```text
previous row 11 -> request A -> accepted = 4
previous row 4  -> request B -> accepted = 3
```

After async remove/add/condense, iteration N+1 has:

```text
current row 0 -> request A -> previous row 11
current row 1 -> request C -> new request
current row 2 -> request B -> previous row 4

prev_positions = [11, -1, 4]
```

If mutable InputBatch row 11 has already been reset/reused to `1`, gathering from InputBatch produces:

```text
buggy:    [1, 1, 3]
expected: [4, 1, 3]
```

Request A then uses a state-copy offset that is three tokens too small.

### Why this is not #45100 or #43559

- #45100 fixed the equivalent async accepted-count race for **non-align** mode by keeping that path device-authoritative. Its implementation intentionally leaves align mode on the synchronized CPU path because align preprocessing consumes CPU-side counts. The ownership problem above remains in that excluded branch.
- #43559 and its follow-up fixes address MTP + prefix-cache chunk/block alignment and poisoned cached Mamba state. This issue concerns previous-iteration accepted-count ownership across async InputBatch row mutation; it can corrupt the state-copy offset even when cached chunk boundaries are correct.

### Cross-backend runtime evidence

The same state-mapping failure was reproduced on the vLLM-Ascend runner, which follows this vLLM model-runner/InputBatch contract:

- issue and controlled reproduction: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/13863
- main fix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13864
- release fix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13865

Observed controlled stress results there:

```text
unfixed accepted-count ownership: intermittent corrupted outputs
independent snapshot/remap:        512/512 correct at 98.82% peak KV usage
```

This is supporting evidence for the shared software-state diagnosis, not a claim that the latest CUDA `main` runtime has already been reproduced on GPU.

### Expected behavior

Previous-iteration accepted counts must remain indexed by the previous iteration until they are remapped through `prev_positions`. Current InputBatch row mutation must not overwrite or race with that historical data.

### Suggested fix

Use the runner-owned `self.num_accepted_tokens.cpu` buffer as the previous-iteration snapshot for async scheduling:

1. For async postprocess, copy accepted counts into the independent runner CPU buffer instead of InputBatch.
2. After the existing event synchronization, gather the snapshot through `prev_positions`.
3. Initialize new requests (`prev_position == -1`) to `1`.
4. Write the remapped current-row values back to InputBatch.
5. Preserve current upstream InputBatch ownership for non-async scheduling, where `condense()` must move accepted counts with current requests.

This reuses the existing `CpuGpuBuffer`, D2H/H2D traffic, and event synchronization; it should not allocate KV cache or require a new synchronization point.

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] I searched open issues and PRs for `postprocess_mamba_align_gpu`, `num_accepted_tokens`, async Mamba align races, InputBatch condensation, and Qwen MTP garbled output.
- [x] I reviewed related #45100 and #43559 and described the difference above.

title: [Bug]: verbose_json crashes when a Whisper chunk emits only EOS
body: `verbose_json` calls `_get_verbose_segments` once, with `FINAL_ONLY` output. A silent Whisper chunk often generates only EOS, and that token stays in `token_ids`. The helper strips a trailing EOS and then reads `tokens_with_start[-2]`. After the strip the sequence is empty, so the request raises `IndexError` instead of returning no segments.

title: [Feature]: [Rust Frontend][Multimodal] Add Gemma 4 image support / multimodal model spec
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### Summary

Please add multimodal/image support for **Gemma 4** models to the Rust frontend's multimodal model/processor registry.

I am serving:

```text
google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it
```

with the vLLM Rust frontend enabled.

vLLM's inference engine correctly recognizes the model as multimodal and initializes the vision/encoder path, but the Rust frontend does not have a multimodal model spec registered for `model_type="gemma4"`.

As a result, the Rust frontend disables image/video support during startup and subsequently rejects otherwise valid OpenAI-compatible `image_url` content with HTTP 400.

This appears closely related to the model-family coverage item tracked in #44280.

---

## Environment

```text
vLLM version: 0.28.0
Model: google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it
Served model name: gemma-4-26b-a4b-it
Frontend: Rust frontend
Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions
```

Relevant multimodal configuration:

```text
limit_mm_per_prompt = {"image": 4, "video": 0}
```

The model is resolved by the vLLM engine as:

```text
Resolved architecture: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration
```

---

## Relevant startup logs

The Rust frontend reports:

```text
(RustFrontend) WARNING [multimodal.rs:446]
multimodal model spec is not registered; disabling image/video support for this model
model_id="google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it" model_type="gemma4"

(RustFrontend) WARNING [multimodal.rs:413]
no multimodal modality resolved; disabling multimodal support for this model
model_id="google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it" model_type="gemma4"
```

However, the engine itself clearly initializes the multimodal portions of Gemma 4:

```text
Resolved architecture: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration
```

and:

```text
Forcing --disable_chunked_mm_input for models with multimodal-bidirectional attention.
```

and later:

```text
Encoder cache will be initialized with a budget of 8192 tokens,
and profiled with 29 image items of the maximum feature size.
```

There is also a `SiglipImageProcessor` initialization message:

```text
[transformers] `SiglipImageProcessorFast` is deprecated.
The `Fast` suffix for image processors has been removed;
use `SiglipImageProcessor` instead.
```

This makes it appear that the inference engine supports the Gemma 4 multimodal path, while the Rust frontend independently disables multimodal request handling because `gemma4` is missing from its image model/processor registry.

---

## Reproduction

Start `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` with the Rust frontend enabled.

Relevant configuration:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1
```

Serve the model with image inputs enabled, e.g.:

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
  --served-model-name gemma-4-26b-a4b-it \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":4,"video":0}'
```

Then send an OpenAI-compatible multimodal chat request:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "What is in this image?"
          },
          {
            "type": "image_url",
            "image_url": {
              "url": "https://vllm-public-assets.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/vision_model_images/2560px-Gfp-wisconsin-madison-the-nature-boardwalk.jpg"
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

The Rust frontend returns:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "unsupported multimodal content: image_url",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "invalid_request_error"
  }
}
```

The request is rejected by the frontend rather than reaching multimodal inference.

---

## Expected behavior

Since `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` is a vision-capable model and vLLM's engine resolves and initializes its multimodal components, I would expect the Rust frontend to recognize `gemma4` as an image-capable model and accept standard OpenAI-compatible content such as:

```json
{
  "type": "image_url",
  "image_url": {
    "url": "https://..."
  }
}
```

Ideally, Gemma 4 would be added to the Rust frontend's registered multimodal model/processor specs.

---

## Relationship to the Rust frontend roadmap

I found #44280, **Rust Frontend Feature Parity**, which describes multimodal support as including an image path for registered image model specs and separately tracks broader model-family coverage beyond the current image processor registry.

This issue seems to be a concrete example of that remaining coverage gap:

```text
Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration
        |
        | engine recognizes multimodal model
        v
vLLM engine / vision encoder
        ✅

Rust frontend multimodal registry
        |
        | model_type="gemma4" not registered
        v
image/video support disabled
        ❌

/v1/chat/completions
        |
        v
"unsupported multimodal content: image_url"
```

I did not find a separate existing issue specifically tracking Gemma 4 multimodal support in the Rust frontend, so I am opening this separately from #44280 in case a model-specific implementation/tracking issue is useful.

---

## Alternatives

The current workaround is to use the Python frontend instead of the Rust frontend for Gemma 4 multimodal serving.

That works around the frontend registration gap, but we would prefer to use the Rust frontend in production.

---

## Additional context

I originally encountered this through LiteLLM, but reproduced the same failure by calling vLLM directly, so LiteLLM is not involved in the failure.

The full vLLM startup log also shows that the target Gemma 4 model initializes its multimodal encoder/cache successfully before the Rust frontend begins serving requests.

There is a separate warning related to the Gemma 4 MTP speculative draft model:

```text
Draft model Gemma4MTP does not support external multimodal embeddings.
Embeddings from the target model will not be passed to the drafter;
using text-only draft inputs instead.
```
