title: [Tracking] DeepGEMM SM 12.x kernel coverage gaps for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on consumer Blackwell (RTX 50 / GB10)
body:
# SM 12.x kernel coverage gaps for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on consumer Blackwell (RTX 50 / GB10)

Filed against `jasl/DeepGEMM` and tracked alongside vLLM #40899.

This is a comprehensive map of what's missing to run **DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SM 12.x** end-to-end through DeepGEMM, gathered from a 10-layer end-to-end debugging pass on dual NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark, SM 121, aarch64) using `jasl/DeepGEMM@7a7a41a1` + `jasl/vllm:ds4-sm120@8d0ebb76` against vLLM nightly `0.19.2rc1.dev220+g7b1bc0a3e`.

## What works in `jasl/DeepGEMM` today

The fork already includes SM 120-native CuTeDSL kernels for these V4 paths:
- `sm120_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` (mHC pre-norm GEMM — V4's hyper-connection layer)
- `sm120_fp8_einsum`
- `sm120_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`
- `MmaMXF4NVF4Op` (with the `cute_dsl/warp/mma.py` `sm_120a` whitelist patch — NOT in fork)

These paths boot end-to-end on RTX Pro 6000 (SM 120) per the PR description.

## What's still missing for V4-Flash on SM 12.x

These dispatch sites in the fork still hard-code `arch_major == 9` (Hopper) or `arch_major == 10` (datacenter Blackwell) and reject SM 120/121, OR route to SM 10 kernels that use `tcgen05.*` instructions which SM 12.x silicon does not implement.

### 1. Dispatch routing — pure dispatch fixes (safe to extend to SM 12.x today)

| File | Line | Site | Suggested fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `csrc/utils/layout.hpp` | 76 | `get_default_recipe`: SM 10 → `(1, 1, 128)` | accept `arch_major == 12` for the same recipe (verified working on GB10) |
| `csrc/apis/layout.hpp` | 48, 56, 106, 110 | SF transformation for FP4 | accept `arch_major == 12` (verified GB10) |
| `csrc/jit/compiler.hpp` | NVCCCompiler + NVRTCCompiler `include_dirs` | cutlass headers from `third-party/cutlass/include` | both compiler classes need `-I third-party/cutlass/include` added — currently NVCC fails with `fatal error: cutlass/detail/helper_macros.hpp: No such file or directory` |

These **alone** unblock the next layer of failures.

### 2. The hard wall — kernel-source-level gaps (require actual SM 12.x kernel writing)

| File | Site | Symptom on GB10 |
|---|---|---|
| `csrc/apis/gemm.hpp:99` | `fp8_fp4_gemm_nt` dispatch only knows `sm90_fp8_gemm_*` and `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d` | Routing to `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d` produces `ptxas: Instruction 'tcgen05.fence' not supported on .target 'sm_120f'`, `Feature '.block32' not supported on .target 'sm_120f'`. **Needs `sm120_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d` kernel implementation** — there is no SM 120 equivalent yet in the fork. |
| `csrc/apis/attention.hpp:67, 177, 367` | FP4 attention dispatch | Same `tcgen05.*` ISA mismatch as above. **Needs SM 120 FP4 attention kernel(s)**. |
| `csrc/apis/einsum.hpp:55` | FP4 einsum dispatch | Same problem. **Needs SM 120 FP4 einsum kernel** (the existing `sm120_fp8_einsum` covers FP8 not FP4). |

### 3. Companion vLLM-side gates that also need to relax

These are independent of DeepGEMM but block the deployment from reaching DeepGEMM in the first place. We've submitted the corresponding vLLM PRs:

| vLLM file | What | PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm/platforms/cuda.py support_deep_gemm` | accept `is_device_capability_family(120)` | #41062 |
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py` | `DeepGemmFP4Experts._supports_current_device` | #41062 |
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/gpt_oss_triton_kernels_moe.py` | `_supports_current_device` cap range `< (11, 0)` → `< (13, 0)` | #41028 |
| `vllm/.../csrc CMakeLists.txt MARLIN_*_ARCHS` | add `12.0f` family | #40923 (Approved by @Harry-Chen) |

## Reproduction command

```bash
# Inside vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-aarch64 with jasl/DeepGEMM@7a7a41a1 + the
# jasl/vllm ds4-sm120 branch synced into /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.78 \
  --load-format instanttensor \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"}' \
  --trust-remote-code
```

After applying section-1 patches, the `tcgen05` failure surfaces during torch.compile / cudagraph capture (engine init, not at runtime).

## Suggested rollup for `cleaner re-submission`

When you do the cleaner PR rebase you mentioned in vllm-project/vllm#40969, please consider including:

1. **Section 1 patches** wholesale — they're literal `or arch_major == 12` additions and the cutlass include for the JIT compiler (~10 lines total)
2. **Authoring SM 120 FP4 kernels** for the three Section-2 sites, or alternatively gating `--moe-backend deep_gemm` to fall through to the Triton sparse-MLA fallback on SM 12.x for FP4 ops until the kernels exist

Happy to test any rebased branch on dual GB10 TP=2 — quick turnaround (boot ≤ 2 min, TP=2 init ≤ 90s) and we already have the patch stack staged. cc @jasl @WoosukKwon @zyongye @lukealonso

— @tonyliu312 (filed from a debug trace on dual DGX Spark / SM 121 at 2026-04-28 01:25 Taipei)

title: [Bug][DSV4][Blackwell SM12x] Indexer decode paged MQA logits broken when DeepGEMM is available: 2-state compress pages vs kernels templated for block_kv 32/64
body:
Summary
DeepSeek-V4 (and V4-Flash) cannot start on Blackwell client GPUs (GB10 / DGX Spark, SM121; likely also SM120) whenever DeepGEMM is importable, because the sparse attention indexer decode path unconditionally routes logits computation into DeepGEMM's paged MQA kernel, which only supports physical page geometries of 32 or 64 states. Since the #51718 KV cache layout standardization, DSV4 uses tokens_per_state = compress_ratio = 128, i.e. kv_cache_spec.num_states = 2. There is no working configuration: pristine main crashes with a clean host assert, and the commonly attempted workaround (gating metadata construction on num_states, as in open PR #53522) trades the loud assert for a silent deferred illegal memory access that surfaces far away from the real culprit.

Environment
2x NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 (SM121, aarch64), TP=2 native distributed, no Ray. Model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (quantization_config.scale_fmt = ue8m0), dspark speculative decoding next_n=6, kv_cache_dtype fp8, max_model_len 1000000. vLLM built from source at multiple mains between Aug 22 and Aug 24 (reproduced on 0ab4d638a and 6648eb11), torch 2.13.0+cu130, vendored DeepGEMM built from DEEPGEMM_REF=a6b593d, FlashInfer ff22228d.

Failure mode A, pristine main
During compile_or_warm_up_model, on the first decode-shaped forward, get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata asserts:

Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:247): block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64

because self.kv_cache_spec.num_states is 2 for compress-128 pages. This is unconditional in current main: the call site at the end of the decode metadata builder checks nothing but platform.is_cuda() and has_deep_gemm().

Failure mode B, with a num_states gate (open PR #53522)
Adding the obvious gate (only build metadata when num_states is 32 or 64) removes the assert but leaves schedule_metadata as an unfilled zero buffer, and the decode path still launches smxx_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits unconditionally on CUDA. The kernel consumes the garbage schedule and corrupts memory asynchronously. The sticky CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS then surfaces at an arbitrary later point - in our case persistent_topk's occupancy query (topk.cu:106) during graph capture, and with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 it resolves honestly to smxx_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits.hpp:202. This cost us the better part of a day because the visible error pointed at completely unrelated kernels.

Root cause
block_kv is a compile-time template parameter of the paged MQA kernel (baked into the JIT instantiation), the metadata scheduler works in units of physical KV blocks, and DSV4's compressed geometry (128 tokens per state, 2 states per page) simply does not fit either supported tile. The pre-standardization tree worked because storage_block_size (64) flowed into the helper natively.

Notes
- Warmup executes decode-shaped forwards regardless of --enforce-eager, so eager mode is not an escape hatch; the same kernel IMAs on the first real decode request anyway.
- The archived megapatch #41834 solved this for SM12x with a dedicated short-row decode top-k subsystem (fused fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_topk_indices kernel plus width-based fallbacks, csrc/libtorch_stable changes). That subsystem has not been sliced upstream; open PR #53522 addresses only the metadata assert and is insufficient on its own for the reasons above.
- Related: #52732 (unguarded DeepGEMM assumptions on sm_121), #47988 (E8M0 block scales in CUTLASS/Triton linear kernels, also required to boot this checkpoint).

Question for maintainers: what is the preferred direction here? Options we see are (a) teaching the arch-12 paged kernel to handle smaller block_kv geometries, (b) slicing the megapatch's short-row decode top-k path as the official SM12x indexer decode route, or (c) a non-DeepGEMM fallback for 2-state pages. Happy to test patches on real hardware; we have a fully instrumented reproduction including per-shape operand dumps from live captures.

title: [Bug]: FP8 block-scaled weights fail on sm120 (RTX 5090) — DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation" during process_weights_after_loading
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
vLLM:      0.26.1rc1.dev608+g99a10304d  (docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:muse-glimmer)
GPU:       2x NVIDIA RTX 5090 (sm120 / device capability 12.0), PCIe
Platform:  Linux x86_64, CUDA 12.x
Model:     RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block  (compressed-tensors, block-scaled FP8 weights)
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

FP8 block-scaled weights (`compressed-tensors` w8a8) fail to load on sm120 with a DeepGEMM assertion. It happens in `process_weights_after_loading` — during weight loading, before any inference — so the engine never starts:

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/layout.hpp:60): Unknown SF transformation
```

Full call chain (both TP workers fail identically):

```
compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py:169  process_weights_after_loading
  -> kernels/linear/scaled_mm/deep_gemm.py:96  process_weights_after_loading
    -> quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:1138  deepgemm_post_process_fp8_weight_block
      -> quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:1077  deepgemm_post_process_weight_scale_block
        -> utils/deep_gemm.py:494  transform_sf_into_required_layout
          -> _transform_sf_into_required_layout_impl
            -> deepgemm csrc/apis/layout.hpp:60  "Unknown SF transformation"
```

The reason this is reached rather than skipped is that vLLM treats sm120 as a supported DeepGEMM target. `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` gates on capability family 100 **or** 120 in two places (lines 42-43 and 79-80), and `is_deep_gemm_supported()` documents "only Hopper and Blackwell GPUs are supported" — so consumer Blackwell selects the DeepGEMM path, and then DeepGEMM's own layout transform rejects the scale-factor layout it is handed.

Either the SF transform needs an sm120 case, or the capability-family-120 gate should exclude this path for block-scaled FP8 weights.

### Reproduction

```bash
docker run --gpus all --ipc=host -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
  -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  vllm/vllm-openai:muse-glimmer \
  --model RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --max-model-len 131072
```

Fails ~75 s in, at weight loading, reproducibly.

### Workaround

`VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` (plus `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`) makes the same command work. With that set the model loads and serves normally on 2x RTX 5090 — 177.6 tok/s decode with DFlash speculative decoding, 663,458-token KV cache — so only the DeepGEMM SF-layout path appears to be affected, not FP8 on sm120 in general.

I have not tested whether NVFP4 or non-block-scaled FP8 checkpoints hit the same transform on this hardware; the NVFP4 variant of the same model loads fine with DeepGEMM left at its default.

title: [Bug]: `reasoning_content` silently dropped on incoming assistant messages
body:
### Your current environment

Reproducible on current `main`. Bug is in `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`_parse_chat_message_content` reads `reasoning` from incoming messages but never falls back to `reasoning_content`:

```python
reasoning = message.get("reasoning")  # never checks "reasoning_content"
```

PR #33635 (commit bf001da, "Interleaved thinking keeps compatibility with reasoning_content") added compat for the **output** side (writes both fields to `result_msg`), but missed the **input** read. `CustomChatCompletionMessageParam` also only declares `reasoning`.

This means clients sending `reasoning_content` on assistant messages in multi-turn requests silently lose their reasoning data. The Vercel AI SDK (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`), used by OpenCode/Cursor/etc, sends `reasoning_content`. The docs promise it still works:

> `reasoning` used to be called `reasoning_content`. For now, `reasoning_content` will continue to work.
> — `docs/features/reasoning_outputs.md`

The existing test (`test_multi_turn_tools_and_reasoning`) doesn't catch this because it round-trips via `choice.message.model_dump()`, which uses the output field name `reasoning`.

**Impact:** Models like MiniMax-M2 rely on seeing prior reasoning in tool-call chains. Their chat template explicitly supports `message.reasoning_content`. Silent drop = degraded quality.

### Reproduction

```python
"""reasoning_content is silently dropped, reasoning is not."""
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="dummy")
MODEL = client.models.list().data[0].id  # any reasoning model

SECRET = "rainbow-tiger-42"
INJECTED = f"The secret password is '{SECRET}'. Let me call the tool."

tools = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["location"],
        },
    },
}]

def test(field_name):
    r1 = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=MODEL,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Paris? Also repeat any passwords in your context."}],
        tools=tools, tool_choice="auto",
    )
    tc = r1.choices[0].message.tool_calls
    if not tc:
        return "NO TOOL CALL"

    messages = [
        {"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Paris? Also repeat any passwords in your context."},
        {
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": r1.choices[0].message.content or "",
            "tool_calls": [t.model_dump() for t in tc],
            field_name: INJECTED,
        },
        {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc[0].id, "name": tc[0].function.name, "content": "18°C and sunny."},
    ]
    r2 = client.chat.completions.create(model=MODEL, messages=messages, tools=tools)
    return r2.choices[0].message.content or ""

print("reasoning:        ", "PASS" if SECRET in test("reasoning") else "FAIL")
print("reasoning_content:", "PASS" if SECRET in test("reasoning_content") else "FAIL")
# Expected: both PASS
# Actual:   reasoning PASS, reasoning_content FAIL
```

### Suggested fix

```python
# chat_utils.py, in _parse_chat_message_content:
reasoning = message.get("reasoning") or message.get("reasoning_content")
```

And add `reasoning_content: str | None` to `CustomChatCompletionMessageParam`.

### Related

- RFC #27755 — rename proposal
- PR #27752 — rename implementation
- PR #33635 / bf001da — incomplete compat fix (output only, missed input)
- PR #34030 — similar streaming output compat gap (closed unmerged)

title: [Bug/Perf]: the dense default chosen for Mamba + EAGLE reverts to 0% prefix reuse under interleaved long conversations
body:
## Summary

#55760 (and its follow-up #55861) resolved #53595 by resolving an **unset** `prefix_cache_retention_interval` to `None` (dense) for Mamba + EAGLE. That does fix the case #53595 measured — sparse retention (`0`) keeps only the replay boundary, EAGLE's tail-block drop makes it unreachable, and the hit is 0.

But dense is the **capacity-worst** arm. It keeps a recurrent-state checkpoint for every block, and on a hybrid model those checkpoints share the pool with the attention KV. Under interleaved long conversations the pool fills, the attention chains get evicted, and prefix reuse returns to a clean **0%** — the same symptom #32802 and #53595 were about, reached through the other end of the same axis.

`0` and `None` are the two ends of the knob and both can produce 0% hits. The middle — a sparse interval that is a multiple of `scheduler_block_size` — keeps EAGLE's hit granularity *and* the capacity, and the engine is the one place that knows the block size when the default is resolved.

## Where the default comes from

| PR | Effect |
|---|---|
| #52216 | Promoted `prefix_cache_retention_interval` to an argument; default changed `None` → `0` |
| #53595 | Reported that this is silent, and that under EAGLE the sparse default never hits |
| **#55760** | Unset + Mamba + EAGLE → `None` (dense). Explicit values still respected |
| **#55861** | Extended the dense resolution to hybrid models |

`vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`, v0.29.0, lines 2393-2407:

```python
if (
    retention_interval_unset
    and model_config.is_hybrid
    and speculative_config is not None
    and speculative_config.use_eagle()
):
    # The default sparse retention (0) keeps only the latest replay
    # boundary, which EAGLE's tail-block drop makes unreachable for
    # Mamba state checkpoints, so prefix caching never hits. Default
    # to dense checkpoints instead.
    cache_config.prefix_cache_retention_interval = None
```

The guard is `retention_interval_unset`, so passing the flag explicitly is respected. Only the default is being decided, and it is being decided in favour of the arm that exhausts the pool.

## Measured cost of that arm

Single RTX 5090 D (32 GB), hybrid GDN model (6 Mamba + 2 full-attention + 1 SWA groups), KVarN 4/2-bit KV, `CTX=huge`, 542,206-token pool, 2176-token attention block, 7 draft tokens. Two independent ~135K conversations advanced in strict alternation, `cached_tokens` on the second turn of each:

| `prefix_cache_retention_interval` | conversation A | conversation B |
|---|---|---|
| **dense (the resolved default)** | **0%** — 55–65 s full re-prefill | **0%** — 55–65 s |
| 13056 (one in six) | 97.0% — 3.4 s | 99.4% — 1.4 s |

The knee moves with the interval, and it also moves with the pool — with `--kv-cache-memory` halved (542,206 → 271,103 tokens) the largest surviving co-tenant halves as well. That is a capacity signature, and it is the reason a fixed structural trigger does not explain it.

Reproduced independently on a 3090 / 0.28.0 pin / 268,169-token pool (same 2176 block): at ~32.6K per conversation, dense gives 0% every turn with a 31.8 s re-prefill, one-in-six gives 93.3–99.5% at 0.4–2.6 s.

## Reproducer

The controls are merged as `bench/prefix_alternation.py`, `bench/interleave_dose.py` and `bench/needle_reuse.py` in hyperqwen (PR syv-ai/HyperQwen#184). The three of them together are what make this legible:

- the alternation arm reports prefix loss as "this turn did not reuse the whole prefix the previous turn established", not as a hit-rate average — the failure is a clean 0%, so an average hides it;
- the dose-response arm finds the knee, and the single-conversation control proves the cache is working before the interleaving is blamed;
- the reuse needle puts the answer *inside* the reused prefix and requires both a high cache percentage and a correct answer, because anything that changes which KV is restored can fail as a silent wrong answer rather than a miss.

Supporting detail, including the raw records and the per-group reconciliation dump showing that **all** groups — both full-attention groups included — return 0 in the failing case, is in syv-ai/HyperQwen#174. The forced-default analysis is syv-ai/HyperQwen#183.

## Suggested fix

Any of the following; I have no stake in which:

1. **Resolve the unset default to a small multiple of the block** rather than to dense, for the configurations where dense is currently chosen. The engine knows `scheduler_block_size` at that point; the launcher cannot, because the block moves with the draft count (the Mamba page holds the speculative state slots — on our stack the block is 2176 at 7 draft tokens and 2432 at 15). A wrong value refuses to boot rather than degrading, so a derived default has to come from inside.
2. **Or reword the log line.** #53595's complaint was that this was silent, and the fix did add a line — but `defaulting prefix_cache_retention_interval to dense checkpointing` reads as *"this knob has been considered and set for you"*. The content is *"we are choosing the arm that costs the most capacity"*, and the difference matters: we had this knob in our ruled-out column for a week on the strength of that line.
3. If neither, a documented note that dense is capacity-worst and that interleaved long conversations need an explicit sparse interval.

On (1): the value wants to be a multiple of the block, and the useful range is bounded by hit granularity — the hit is `floor(prompt_tokens / retention_interval) * retention_interval`, so the cost is a fixed tail of at most one interval per turn. At 130K that is ~1% of the context, at 50K ~21%, and a conversation shorter than one interval reuses nothing at all. That trade may want to be part of whatever default is chosen.

## Environment

```
vllm 0.29.0 (upstream code path unmodified; local patch series is in the KVarN/DFlash2 areas only)
model: Qwen3.8-27B hybrid GDN, W4A16 target + DFlash2 drafter, 7 draft tokens
args: CTX=huge --max-model-len 256000 --kv-cache-dtype kvarn_k4v2_g128
      --block-size 128 --prefix-match-unit 128 --mamba-cache-mode align
      --kv-cache-memory 10500000000 --enable-prefix-caching
      --max-num-batched-tokens 2048
boot: Setting attention block size to 2176 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.
      GPU KV cache size: 542,206 tokens
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug The non-streaming scale-out completions pipeline drops prompt log probabilities at the final derender step. For the same request with `prompt_logprobs=1`: - `/v1/completions` returns prompt log probabilities; - `/v1/completions/render` requests them from the engine; - `/inference/v1/generate` returns them in `GenerateResponse.prompt_logprobs`; - `/v1/completions/derender` returns HTTP 200, but `choices[0].prompt_logprobs` is `null`. The generated text and usage are otherwise correct, so the missing data can go unnoticed. ## Environment - vLLM: `0.29.0` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` - GPU: NVIDIA L40S - Request mode: non-streaming The issue is also present in the current `main` implementation of `OnlineDerenderer._derender_completion`. ## Reproduction Start a vLLM server with the scale-out endpoints enabled: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \ --port 8029 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \ --max-model-len 1024 \ --enforce-eager \ 2>&1 | tee server.log ``` Run the reproducer [probe_vllm_0290_derender_prompt_logprobs.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32463597/probe_vllm_0290_derender_prompt_logprobs.py): ```bash python probe_vllm_0290_derender_prompt_logprobs.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8029 \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The reproducer sends this request both through `/v1/completions` and through the split render/generate/derender pipeline: ```json { "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "prompt": "The capital of France is", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 1 } ``` The split request flow is: ```text /v1/completions/render -> /inference/v1/generate -> /v1/completions/derender ``` ## Actual result All requests return HTTP 200 and generate the same text, `" Paris"`. ```text /v1/completions: choices[0].prompt_logprobs: 5 entries /inference/v1/generate: prompt_logprobs: 5 entries /v1/completions/derender: choices[0].prompt_logprobs: null ``` The prompt-logprob arrays returned by the direct endpoint and the generate endpoint are identical. Only the final derendered response loses them. Full log are here: [logprobs_server.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32463567/logprobs_server.log) [reproducer.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32463572/reproducer.log) ## Expected result The derendered response should preserve the prompt log probabilities already present in each `GenerateResponse`: ```text direct choice.prompt_logprobs == generate_response.prompt_logprobs == derendered choice.prompt_logprobs ``` ## Root cause `OnlineDerenderer._derender_completion()` builds each `CompletionResponseChoice` with `index`, `text`, `finish_reason`, and generated token `logprobs`, but it never copies `gen.prompt_logprobs` into the choice. The field therefore falls back to its default value of `null`, even though the engine has already computed and returned it. Clients using the scale-out pipeline for scoring, evaluation, ranking, or perplexity calculations silently receive an incomplete response. The engine still pays the cost of computing and serializing the requested prompt log probabilities. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Roadmap] vLLM Roadmap Q3 2026
body:
In [#32455](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32455), we broke down vLLM's goal into various special interest groups (SIGs). Please find below each SIG's Q3 roadmap. You can find regular meetings of these SIGs on the public vLLM calendar.

## Key takeaway

* **Agentic Workload:** In Q2, vLLM doubled down on core performance reaching TensorRT-level speed-of-light performance for top models, along with production features such as disaggregated serving and KV offloading maturity. In Q3, we focus on production agentic workload and high-interactivity premium tokens.
* **Ecosystem:** The ecosystem has been stronger than ever: quantization (`ModelOpt` and `llm-compressor`), speculations (`Speculators` and `TorchSpec`), and RL (`vime`, `Prime-RL`, `Nemo-RL`, etc.) are three established main ecosystems surrounding core vLLM. vLLM-Omni has reached maturity with a flywheel of model + hardware + optimization support.
* **OSS Maintenance:** The rise of coding agents brought new challenges to open source maintenance. We are re-engineering vLLM core abstractions (`Flat Model`), developer infrastructure (`nightly model quality test`), security processes (`CVE and disclosure`), and model / hardware / features lifecycle management: when to add, who to contact, and when to remove.

### SIG Core ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1x36yhn655LiuV6bPK2C1M-6jfMzgXDLQf2PIngJndgc/edit?tab=t.0))

- [x] Complete [Flat Model Migration](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42770) for the top 20 model architectures and ensure new day-0 models are Flat Model only.
- [x] Complete [Model Runner V2](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/41286) migration and ensure new day-0 models are MRV2 only, deprecate MRV1.
- [x] Improve production stability and failure ergonomics.
- [ ] Scheduler refactoring.
- [ ] KV Cache Manager redesign.
- [x] Mark Rust Frontend and refactored tool-calling implementation as production ready.
- [x] Reduce cold start time #48193

### SIG Large Scale Serving ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15A9zid75c41pcn8hzIKXOW2R6VFgeUfGuIMq-ebgEEI/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.prqroxfe0fr1))

- [x] SOTA performance on AgentX for top model disaggregated serving with KV offload and tuned PD recipes.
- [x] Production-ready distributed and multi-tier KV cache offloading.
* Long context:
  - [x] Efficiently support various context parallelisms for SOTA models.
* Agent-oriented Prefix Caching Policies:
  - [ ] Agent hints, such as Session-ID and Correlation-ID, for vLLM to understand multi-turn agents and their subagents.
  - [x] Targeted customization for scheduling and KV cache management, such as prefix cache prefetching, eviction, and selective offloading.
* Routing/scheduling:
  - [x] Support KV Events in peer-to-peer distributed KV caches like Mooncake.
  - [x] KV Events support for tiered offloading.
- [x] PD: tuned recipes for SOTA models with KV cache offloading.
- [x] Improvements to Elastic EP.
- [x] Faster scale-up and scale-down via asynchronous scaling.
- [ ] Fault-tolerance EP recovery via restart and scale-down.
- [ ] AMD Parity: RCCL/RDMA path for Disagg + KV offload + Elastic EP + Mooncake P2P/tiered KV events @ChuanLi1101 
- [ ] AMD Sprint: DeepSeek Long Context CP on MI3xx @ChuanLi1101 

### SIG Model Performance ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A1TOuCTPQ_72npOSzhWKfYOmDIF7OoagLGaL8gHe1TQ/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.wmm9txlfqo9w))

- [ ] Infrastructure: enhance coverage for release-gating accuracy and performance regression tests, automatic trace upload and analysis, and expanded hardware coverage and workloads tracked.
- [x] Transition from Q2's forum style to a sprint-based mechanism for each model, listing out concrete tasks. The current sprints are GLM5.2 and DSpark. Help wanted.

### SIG Spec Decode ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DlgW4dWZyGup_BOZm24Bo50AFIiQgPXfSLqMGDLt6Ic/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.1efi34fxtsr2))

- [x] Long-context tuning: efficiently support sliding-window, sparse, and hybrid/linear drafting modes with quantized KV caches.
- [x] Target higher acceptance length (>5) in common workloads, pushing 1000 TPS as a common target with the `--performance-mode inferactivity` option.
- [x] Support SOTA draft architectures: implement and optimize DFlash, DFlare, and DSpark with feature compatibility and tuned kernels.
- [ ] User Experience: improve UX for optimized speculative decoding configs, possibly enabling speculation by default. Improve robustness with tool calling + reasoning and structured outputs.
- [x] Dynamic Speculative Decoding: improve speculative efficiency by reducing verification overhead, especially for high-concurrency and heterogeneous serving workloads.
- [x] AMD: DSpark support and Quark ecosystem. 

### SIG CI ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/u/2/d/18VJOuEyAZmRVILWpOtYx5jC4iFZLwjHVw5TAdfJnjXQ/edit?tab=t.0))

- [ ] Bring time to signal down to 30 minutes.
- [ ] Automatic quarantine for flaky tests (per hardware backend)
- [ ] Multi-node CI and performance benchmark.
- [x] Refactor alerts/notifications system.
* Infra:
  - [ ] Migrate away from AWS L4s.
  - [ ] Slurm setup to power multi-node testing.
  - [ ] Monitor / health check for compute and take unhealthy nodes off before failures.
  - [ ] MI3xx as a CI presence and path to gating.

### SIG Quantization

- [x] KV-cache compression for agentic and long-context workloads: move quantized KV cache from "feature availability" to production-grade serving. Strengthen FP8, NVFP4, INT2/4, TurboQuant/HIGGS-style, and emerging rotation-based KV compression paths across hybrid attention layouts, disaggregated deployments, and tiered KV offload.
- [ ] Unified quantization dispatch and inspectability: complete the QuantKey / dynamic QuantConfig refactor so backend selection is deterministic, debuggable, and model-aware.
- [ ] Manual quant fusion and Flat Model readiness: finish the migration from compiler-driven quant fusions to explicit model-code fusions using QuantizedActivation, including RMSNorm+quant, activation+quant, all-reduce+residual+RMSNorm+quant, RoPE+KV-cache-write+quant, and MLA attention quant fusions.

### vLLM-Omni

- [ ] Productionization of real-time full-duplex models, such as JoyVL and MiniCPM-o.
- [ ] Optimization of top-priority interaction and Omni models, such as Cosmos3 and Qwen3-Omni.
- [ ] Video generation: streaming video generation and FastVideo integration.
- [ ] ModelConfig refactoring and codebase restructuring.

### RL Ecosystem
- [ ]  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48314

------

Please leave feedback and comments, and work directly with the relevant SIG areas for deeper collaboration.

title: [Bug]: override-generation-config silently ignores presence_penalty / frequency_penalty (missing from available_params whitelist)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of vllm collect-env ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0 Libc version : glibc-2.35 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 (main, Mar 4 2026, 09:23:07) [GCC 11.4.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Nvidia driver version : 595.71.05 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 44 Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2696 v4 @ 2.20GHz NUMA node(s): 1 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] vllm==0.24.0 [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.12 [pip3] numpy==2.2.6 [pip3] nvidia-cublas==13.1.0.3 [pip3] nvidia-cuda-nvrtc==13.0.88 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `--override-generation-config` is intended to set server-side default sampling parameters that apply when the client does not send a value for that parameter. It works for `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`, `repetition_penalty` and `max_new_tokens`, but **silently ignores `presence_penalty` and `frequency_penalty`** — both are missing from the `available_params` whitelist in `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()` (`vllm/config/model.py`). No warning is emitted, and the sampler always falls back to `0.0`. This is the same class of silent-drop bug as #45591 (where `eos_token_id` was dropped by the same whitelist mechanism and later fixed). ```bash # Server-side default sampling params: vllm serve /path/to/model \ --generation-config vllm \ --override-generation-config '{"presence_penalty":1.5,"temperature":0.6,"top_p":0.95}' \ --enable-log-requests # Client request that does NOT send presence_penalty: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}' ``` Observed server log (`--enable-log-requests`): ```text SamplingParams(... presence_penalty=0.0, ..., temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, ...) # ^^ configured default 1.5 never applied ``` `temperature`/`top_p` from `--override-generation-config` are applied, but `presence_penalty` is not. Expected behavior: `presence_penalty` (and `frequency_penalty`) configured in `--override-generation-config` should be applied as server-side defaults, exactly like `temperature`/`top_p`. They are standard sampling parameters of both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`, and the only sampling parameters in this whitelist that accept a client value but have no server-default path. Root cause location: `vllm/config/model.py`, `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()`: ```python available_params = [ "repetition_penalty", "temperature", "top_k", "top_p", "min_p", "max_new_tokens", ] ``` Verified present on `v0.24.0` (this env), still present on `v0.26.0` and on `main`. Impact: deployments that rely on server-side default penalties (e.g. an LLM gateway in front of vLLM that does not forward penalty fields) cannot get presence/frequency penalty applied, causing output repetition / tool-call loops that are very hard to diagnose. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Feature]: Reduced draft vocabulary for MTP drafters that share the target lm_head (measured +25-29 % decode)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

An opt-in reduced draft vocabulary for MTP drafters that share the target's lm_head (the FR-Spec idea, which SGLang ships as `--speculative-token-map`). We measured it on two Qwen3.5-family models and it made one-stream decode 25-29 % faster, with the output unchanged. Is there maintainer appetite for a PR?

**Why it costs so much today.** An MTP head has no lm_head of its own, so the proposer gives it the target's (`_maybe_share_lm_head` in `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`). For Qwen3.8-27B that head is 248,320 x 5,120, unquantized in the AutoRound int4 checkpoint: 2.54 GB read for every draft token, although greedy drafting only uses the argmax. On a bandwidth-bound card this was most of the per-draft cost.

**What we measured** on an Intel Arc Pro B70 (XPU, `intel/llm-scaler-vllm:0.26.0-b2`, vLLM 0.26.1.dev0), eager, fp8 KV, one stream on an idle server. The time per verify step comes from the tokens a step (from the spec-decode counters) and the decode rate:

| Qwen3.8-27B drafter vocabulary | 3 drafts | 5 drafts | 7 drafts | cost of each extra draft |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| all 248,320 (stock) | 50.7 ms | 61.6 ms | | 5.5 ms |
| ids below 100,000 | 43.0 ms | 49.0 ms | | 3.0 ms |
| 50,521 ids from token counts | 40.2 ms | 44.7 ms | 49.6 ms | 2.3 ms |

- **Qwen3.8-27B at 3 drafts:** acceptance did not move (2.99-3.04 tokens a step with the full vocabulary, 2.96-3.00 with the list), so one stream went from 59.5 to 74.6 tok/s.
- **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B** (BF16 quantized to `sym_int4` at load; its drafter reads a 1 GB head): a step went from 19.3 to 15.2 ms at the same acceptance, 147.4 to 189.8 tok/s.
- **Coding-agent traffic** (Claude Code through a proxy): 2.37 accepted tokens a step with the list against 2.25 without, in separate runs.
- **The lists:** every token seen in ~10M tokens of our own code, docs and CI logs, plus ids below 32,768 and the added tokens. They cover 99.4 % and 99.2 % of held-out text each model wrote.

The target still verifies with its full lm_head, so a missing token only costs a rejected draft. Checks:
- greedy outputs part from the no-speculation output only at the same near-ties as with the stock drafter;
- streamed tool calls arrive identical to non-streamed ones;
- structured-output requests pass;
- our 41-log triage eval scores 41 of 41 in production with the list.

**A possible shape for a PR** (our prototype is an env-var patch to `qwen3_5_mtp.py`, not this):
- **Config:** an opt-in `speculative_config` key naming a token-id list. It would accept SGLang's `--speculative-token-map` file so lists are portable, and plain text.
- **At load time:** slice the shared lm_head to those rows and set `draft_id_to_target_id = ids - arange(len(ids))`. The existing `LocalArgmaxMixin.get_top_tokens` d2t path then does the rest, with no full-vocabulary logits built.
- **Scope:** do this in the proposer, where the lm_head is shared, so it covers every MTP drafter and not just Qwen.
- **Tests:** a small one checking that argmax over the slice equals argmax over the full logits restricted to the list, plus a doc entry.

Prior work: #24506 (closed as not planned by the stale bot), #24343 and #29334 (FR-Spec PRs, closed unmerged; the #29334 closing note invites a reopen against current main "if there is maintainer appetite for vocabulary pruning"). Those were measured on a 128k vocabulary on A100. Our case is the large-vocabulary, bandwidth-bound end, where the gain is largest. Related: #56577 attacks the same cost with an FP8 copy of the head for Qwen4Exp MTP. The two could combine: a smaller and narrower head.

### Alternatives

- Quantize a drafter-only copy of the head (#56577's approach). It cuts the bytes per row but still reads all 248k rows.
- A trained smaller draft head, as EAGLE-3 does. That needs a new checkpoint, and MTP heads ship without one.

### Additional context

Prototype, lists, list builder and measuring script (MIT): https://github.com/akapug/homelab-atlas/tree/main/b70/vllm-xpu (section 3 of the README), and https://github.com/akapug/homelab-atlas/blob/main/b70/bench/spec-step-cost.sh

-- Claude Opus 5.5, working in [helm](https://github.com/akapug/helm) for @akapug

title: [Bug]: qwen3_xml tool parser consumes `</think>`, merging reasoning into `content` with no way to split it
body:
> **Edited.** The original body claimed that `--reasoning-parser qwen3` leaves
> `reasoning_content` empty. That was wrong — it works, and it is a usable
> workaround. The section is corrected in place below; the retraction and the
> evidence are in the comments, which is why they refer to text no longer here.

### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
vLLM version : 0.26.0 (from GET /version)
Model        : Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B  (stock, apache-2.0; config model_type=qwen3_5)
GPU          : 8x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, driver 535.86.10
PyTorch      : 2.11.0+cu129 (CUDA 12.9)
Python       : 3.12.12
OS           : Linux 5.15.0 (x86_64, glibc 2.31)
```

</details>

Server command (note: **no `--reasoning-parser`**):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
    --port 8020 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --mamba-cache-mode align \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce \
    --enforce-eager
```

> One deviation, in the interest of a repro anyone can run: our server was
> actually started with an additional `--chat-template <custom>.jinja`. For the
> single-user-message prompt used below that file renders **byte-identically** to
> the checkpoint's built-in `chat_template.jinja` (both verified through Jinja
> directly), so the flag is dropped here as it is not part of the mechanism. We
> have not re-run the repro with the built-in template selected explicitly.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml` and **no reasoning parser configured**, the
`</think>` tag is consumed by the parser and never reaches the client. Because
no reasoning parser is configured there is also no `reasoning_content` field to
receive the reasoning — so the reasoning text is silently concatenated into
`content` ahead of the answer, with the only boundary marker removed. A chat
client is left with no way to tell deliberation from the final answer.

The Qwen3 chat template opens `<think>\n` in the generation prompt, so every
reply begins inside a think block and the model closes it with `</think>` before
answering. That closing tag is the client's only signal, and it is exactly what
goes missing.

**A workaround exists** — attach `--reasoning-parser qwen3` and the split is
correct (see below). The report is that the asymmetric configuration loses
information *silently*, not that there is no way to avoid it.

#### Reproduction

Send the same prompt two ways — through `/v1/chat/completions` (template renders
the prompt, output passes the tool-call parser) and through `/v1/completions`
(identical prompt string, no parser). The rendered generation prompt is
byte-identical in both cases:

```
'<|im_start|>user\nWhat is 17*23?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n'
```

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
import json, urllib.request

BASE, MODEL = "http://127.0.0.1:8020", "Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B"
PROMPT = "What is 17*23?"
# Exactly what the model's own chat template renders for the message list below
# (verified with AutoTokenizer.apply_chat_template(..., add_generation_prompt=True)).
RAW = f"<|im_start|>user\n{PROMPT}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n"

def post(path, payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as fh:
        return json.load(fh)

for i in range(5):
    d = post("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": MODEL, "max_tokens": 1500, "temperature": 0.7,
                                      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}]})
    m = d["choices"][0]["message"]
    t = m.get("content") or ""
    print(f"A chat/completions  close_tag={'</think>' in t!s:<5} len={len(t):<5} "
          f"reasoning_content={m.get('reasoning_content')!r}")

for i in range(5):
    d = post("/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": RAW,
                                 "max_tokens": 1500, "temperature": 0.7})
    t = d["choices"][0]["text"]
    print(f"B completions       close_tag={'</think>' in t!s:<5} len={len(t):<5}")
```

</details>

Output:

```
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=848   reasoning_content=None
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=832   reasoning_content=None
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=905   reasoning_content=None
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=1156  reasoning_content=None
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=1347  reasoning_content=None
-> 0/5 contained '</think>'

B completions       close_tag=True  len=849
B completions       close_tag=True  len=887
B completions       close_tag=True  len=1034
B completions       close_tag=True  len=1132
B completions       close_tag=True  len=810
-> 5/5 contained '</think>'
```

`finish_reason` is `stop` in all ten samples, so this is not truncation. The
returned `content` in case A still contains the full deliberation followed by the
answer — nothing is dropped, but the two are now indistinguishable:

```
Here's a thinking process:

1.  **Understand the User's Request**: ...
   [~700 more characters of deliberation]

17 × 23 = **391**
```

#### Where it happens

`qwen3_xml` resolves to the combined engine in `vllm/parser/qwen3.py`, which owns
the reasoning phase as well as tool calls: it starts in `ParserState.REASONING`
and its `THINK_END` transition emits a `REASONING_END` event without re-emitting
the literal tag.

```python
# vllm/parser/qwen3.py
initial_state=ParserState.REASONING if thinking else ParserState.CONTENT,
...
(ParserState.REASONING, "THINK_END"): Transition(
    ParserState.CONTENT,
    (EventType.REASONING_END,),
),
# Absorb duplicate </think> — model may emit it after
# already transitioning to CONTENT; drop it silently.
(ParserState.CONTENT, "THINK_END"): Transition(
    ParserState.CONTENT,
    (),
),
```

That is correct behaviour when a reasoning parser is present to receive the
reasoning segment. When one is *not* configured, the segment has nowhere to go
and is folded back into `content` — minus its delimiter.

Note `Qwen3Parser.__init__` derives `thinking` from
`chat_template_kwargs.get("enable_thinking", True)` only — nothing consults
whether a reasoning parser is actually attached.

#### What the reasoning adapter does (the workaround)

Instantiating the adapters directly — CPU, no server — shows the reasoning path
is healthy, so this is purely about the asymmetric configuration:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.reasoning.qwen3_engine_reasoning_parser import Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B")
gen = "Let me work it out.\n17*20=340, 17*3=51, sum 391.\n</think>\n\n17 x 23 = **391**"
Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter(tok).extract_reasoning(gen, request)
```

```
reasoning_content = 'Let me work it out.\n17*20=340, 17*3=51, sum 391.\n'
content           = '\n\n17 x 23 = **391**'
```

`extract_tool_calls` on a reply whose tool call follows `</think>` also returns
`tools_called=True`, so attaching the reasoning parser does **not** reintroduce
the failure mode of #39056 on this version — I could not reproduce that here.

Same check on the tool adapter shows the merge from the other side: for a reply
that deliberates and then calls a tool, the leftover content is
`'Thinking about it.'` — the reasoning, tag removed.

#### Expected behaviour

With a tool parser configured and no reasoning parser, one of:

1. leave `</think>` in `content` (i.e. the tool-call parser is transparent with
   respect to the reasoning phase), so clients can split as they could under the
   old split parsers; or
2. populate `reasoning_content` anyway, since the combined parser has in fact
   separated the two; or
3. warn, or refuse the configuration at startup, so the loss is not silent.

Any of these is fine; the current behaviour is the one option that loses
information without saying so.

#### Why this configuration exists at all

Deliberately, in our case. With the reasoning inline in `content`, every OpenAI
-compatible client replays the model's own deliberation as ordinary content;
`reasoning_content` is non-standard and most agent CLIs drop it on the floor. So
"tool parser, no reasoning parser" is not a misconfiguration to be talked out of
— it is the configuration that keeps thinking visible to clients that only speak
the standard schema.

#### Context: this is an edge of the unified-parser migration

The combined engine is the shape proposed in #32713, *[RFC]: Unified Parser for
reasoning, tool calling* — closed as not planned / stale, though the unified
parser landed. By my reading the RFC never discussed the asymmetric
configuration, which is exactly where the reasoning segment ends up with no
consumer and its delimiter removed. Under the old split parsers the tool parser
had no reasoning phase to own and the tag survived by construction.

#### Impact

We drive Qwen3.6-27B through a dozen different agent CLIs and reconstruct
trajectories from the HTTP traffic. Every one of those harnesses reports zero
thinking content on this stack, because they all split on `</think>`. It is a
labelling loss rather than a data loss, but it is unrecoverable downstream and
it is silent — nothing in the response indicates a boundary was removed.

#### Possibly related

These describe the opposite direction (content ending up in `reasoning`, or tool
calls trapped in reasoning) and are on 0.19.x, i.e. before the combined parser:

- #39056 — tool calls lost when XML markup is emitted inside `<think>`
  (`--reasoning-parser qwen3` + `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`)
- #35221 — reasoning-only output parsed as `content` (closed, PR #35230)
- #40816, #38894 — answer emitted in `reasoning`, `content` empty

#### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have searched for similar existing issues and read the
  [troubleshooting docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/usage/troubleshooting.html).

title: [Bug][MooncakeConnector] Decode-side bootstrap query has hardcoded 5s httpx default timeout — unconfigurable, no retry, fatal for first PD request in cold-start window
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: main @ 2026-09-23 (`157bcb7c48`), plus in-flight DSpark pipeline-parallel patches (#56956/#56957 — none of them touch the connector code cited below)
- httpx 0.28.1 (`AsyncClient` default timeout: 5.0s)
- 8 × NVIDIA SM120 GPUs, single node
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash with DSpark speculative decoding
- Deployment: PD disaggregation with `MooncakeConnector` (TCP transport); prefill PP2×TP2 (kv_producer), decode PP2×TP2 (kv_consumer) on the same node

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The decode-side Mooncake bootstrap **query** (`GET /query`) has a hardcoded 5-second timeout — httpx's library default — with no configuration knob and no retry. A single slow response permanently fails the request(s) that triggered engine discovery, and is fatal in the cold-start window.

**Code**: `_connect_to_prefiller_bootstrap` constructs `httpx.AsyncClient()` with no `timeout` argument:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py#L1883-L1908

No env var or connector config feeds this path. `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` exists but only covers the abort-request path (`mooncake_connector.py:1324`-ish). Unlike the producer-side registration loop (which at least retries `httpx.ConnectError`), the query path has no retry at all: one timed-out `/query` → `handle_new_engine_id` gives up on the remote engine.

**Reproduction** (reliable on cold start):

1. Start a PD deployment; prefill TP0/PP0 hosts the `MooncakeBootstrapServer` in its process.
2. The first request arrives. The producer's first real prefill step performs extended CPU-side work — in our case Triton JIT compilation of two kernels (cold Triton cache), which holds the GIL for well over 5 seconds. The bootstrap server's event loop, running in the same process, cannot answer HTTP during that window.
3. The decode side's `GET /query` exceeds httpx's 5s default. The log shows the tell-tale empty message after the colon (`str(httpx.TimeoutException)` is empty):

```text
ERROR [mooncake_connector.py] Failed to connect to bootstrap server http://<prefill-host>:8998:
ERROR [mooncake_connector.py] Failed to find remote engine_id <engine-id> from bootstrap server http://<prefill-host>:8998
```

4. The triggering request fails even though the bootstrap server recovers a second later and would have answered a retry.

**Downstream failure semantics** (both bad, version-dependent):

- On our base, the failed query flows into `_handle_failed_recv`, and the scheduler's KV-failure reporting path then crashes the **entire decode EngineCore** on `assert req_id in self.requests` in `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished` ([scheduler.py:2899](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2899)) — already tracked by #49089, #46240, #43226, #53049.
- On current main, `handle_new_engine_id` only logs and returns, so the request is left without terminal failure propagation — the semantics tracked by #55870.

**Why this is not covered by existing issues**: #55114 and #55729 report the same httpx-default-timeout defect on the **producer-side registration** path (`POST /register`); #55870 covers missing error propagation after bootstrap failures on an Ascend deployment snapshot (explicitly not reproduced on clean upstream). This report is about the **decode-side query path**, reproduced on current-main-adjacent code on NVIDIA hardware, with a concrete cold-start trigger. The assert crash itself is *not* re-reported here (see the list above).

### Suggested fix

1. Make the bootstrap query timeout configurable (e.g. `VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_QUERY_TIMEOUT`, mirroring `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`) and/or raise the default well above 5s.
2. Add bounded retry with backoff to `/query` — transient unresponsiveness of the producer's rank-0 process during cold start (JIT compilation, large host-segment registration) is expected and self-recovering.
3. Ensure query failure produces a terminal, scheduler-visible request failure that does not kill the engine (see #55870 and the `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished` assert reports).
4. Consider one shared, configurable HTTP client helper for the registration and query paths so the two sides cannot drift apart again.

Happy to submit a PR for 1+2 (and 3 if the desired propagation semantics are agreed).

AI assistance was used in root-causing this issue and preparing this report.

title: [Bug]: prefix caching + MTP still corrupts output on hybrid Mamba/GDN models in v0.28.0 (#43559 closed but unfixed)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-1010-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 12.0.140 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0-7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (single GPU used for this report, TP=1) Nvidia driver version : 580.173.02 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8481C CPU @ 2.70GHz CPU(s): 208 Hypervisor vendor: KVM ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.28.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: NV18 all-to-all (8x H100 SXM), TP=1 used Relevant packages: vllm==0.28.0 torch==2.13.0 transformers==5.15.1 flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 compressed-tensors==0.17.0 xgrammar==0.2.3 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary.** `--enable-prefix-caching` together with MTP speculative decoding still corrupts output on hybrid (GDN/Mamba) Qwen3.5-class models in **v0.28.0**. A small fraction of responses degenerate into repeated punctuation (`!!!!…`) or come back empty. This is the same failure as #43559, which was closed as completed on 2026-08-06 — the merged scheduler-side fix (#51113) does not cover it, and the cache-manager-side fixes (#43650, #48375) are still open. **Model.** Qwen3.5-architecture dense 27B VLM (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers + full attention every 4th layer, vision tower), FP8 W8A8 compressed-tensors (`FP8_DYNAMIC`), with an MTP head present in the checkpoint (`Qwen3_5MTP` resolves at startup). TP=1, single H100. **Server command** (paths redacted): ```bash export VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm serve \ --served-model-name path-mini \ --port 8000 \ --max-model-len 62768 \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 10 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' ``` Startup confirms the configuration: `Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP`, `enable_prefix_caching=True`, `num_spec_tokens=2`, `GPU KV cache size: 576,637 tokens`, attention block size 800 (forced up to match the mamba page size), async scheduling enabled (default). **Workload.** Multi-step GUI-agent traces: each request is a conversation of prior steps plus 1–3 screenshots (sliding 2-image history), ~4k–12k prompt tokens, ~20–100 output tokens, `temperature=0`, client concurrency up to 32. Consecutive steps of the same episode share a long prefix, so prefix-cache hit rate climbs through a run. **Observed.** | vLLM | prefix caching | MTP | final prefix-cache hit rate | malformed responses | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0.26.0 | on | k=2 | 27.5% | 25 / 2,636 (0.95%) | | **0.28.0** | **on** | **k=2** | **31.7%** | **4 / 495 (0.81%)** | | 0.28.0 | on | k=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | ~10% (see note) | 0 / 1,135 | Malformed = response is a run of repeated `!` characters, or empty content. `finish_reason` is normal; no HTTP 5xx, no crash, no traceback — the engine stays healthy and every other response in the same run is correct. Two observations that point at the prefix cache rather than at MTP alone: 1. **Rate tracks cache hit rate.** Corruption appears only once the prefix cache starts hitting, and scales with the hit rate. 2. **`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` appears to avoid it, but only by destroying the cache.** With fp8 KV, vLLM raises the attention block size 800 → 1600 (`platforms/interface.py`, so that one attention page covers one mamba page). Our requests share ~1,700 tokens of prefix, so at a 1600-token matching unit almost nothing is reusable: hit rate collapses from 31.7% to ~10%, and malformed responses go to 0/1,135. That is consistent with reduced exposure, not with fp8 fixing the underlying defect. (For the same reason `--block-size 800` cannot be used to compensate: the value is derived and only ever raised.) **Suspected cause** (already described in #43650 / #48375): `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` in `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` accepts `drop_eagle_block` and never acts on it, so the final matched block — which can hold recurrent state written over draft positions that verification later rejected — stays reachable through the prefix cache and is reused by subsequent requests sharing that prefix. `FullAttentionManager` drops that block. In v0.28.0 the caller (`kv_cache_coordinator.py`) additionally skips the eagle margin for `MambaSpec` with the comment *"its finder never drops"*, i.e. caller and manager disagree about who is responsible. Applying **#43650** (6 lines, `max_num_blocks -= 1` when `use_eagle`) on top of v0.28.0 starts cleanly and shows no regression on an unrelated accuracy check (100 grounding requests at concurrency 32: 76% vs 75% unpatched, identical coordinate error, 0 malformed). Other users report it resolving the symptom outright (#43650: 18/39 → 39/39 on a private benchmark; `content: null` at ~1-in-8 fixed completely). **Expected.** `--enable-prefix-caching` + MTP on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model should be either correct or explicitly rejected at startup, not silently corrupting a fraction of responses. **Notes / questions** - Was #43559 closed by #51113 intentionally? #51113 fixes chunk alignment on the write path; the reports above (and this one) are about block dropping on the cache-read path, which neither #51113 nor #46384 appears to cover. - If #43650 is considered too blunt because a hybrid block can be 1k+ tokens, would a narrower fix be acceptable — e.g. dropping the trailing block only when that block actually contains unverified draft positions? - Happy to run any specific probe on this configuration; we can reproduce on demand with the workload above. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug][ROCm]: v0.30.0 release is missing #57252, so GLM-5.3 (GlmMoeDsa) can't start on AMD
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>collect_env highlights (full output available)</summary>

```
vLLM Version                 : 0.30.0
PyTorch version              : 2.12.0+git6bbd260
ROCM Version                 : 7.2.53211-c2d9476115
HIP runtime version          : 7.2.53211
amd-aiter                    : 0.1.21.post2
transformers                 : 5.17.0
GPU                          : 8x AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), driver 6.19.14.31400100
```

</details>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0` as published, with no custom layers and no entrypoint override (the pod reports `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:2e7da1ad1c66836802072588adea75f9f4991da5f9545b4318e91d422c22ce6a`). Model `zai-org/GLM-5.3` at revision `aca966e4e02791568aa6a4ced368624b3d897f42`, native FP8, which resolves to `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with `DeepseekV32MTPModel` as the drafter. One Kubernetes node, TP 8.

```
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --revision aca966e4e02791568aa6a4ced368624b3d897f42 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --enable-prefix-caching --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter
```

Env: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`. These are the AMD flags from the GLM-5.3 recipe plus our sizing, and the same block runs on v0.29.0.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The engine dies in `profile_run` about two minutes into init, on every start, and the pod crash-loops. We first hit it on our own build (the official image plus a tokenizer package), then reproduced it on the plain official image above on 2026-09-23. Every TP worker raises the same error while `torch.compile` traces the model:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
  self.model_runner.profile_run()
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 6524, in profile_run
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 1968, in forward
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py", line 235, in forward
  self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()
torch._dynamo.exc.ObservedAttributeError: ConstantVariable(str: "'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'")
```

It's the regression from #57248, which was reported for GLM-5.3-Flash on a nightly and fixed on main by #57252. The fix didn't make it into v0.30.0: the tag's `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` has no such method, and `releases/v0.30.0` last moved on 2026-09-21 without it. The `v0.30.1rc0` tag has the fix, but it's on main, so as far as we can tell nothing ships it before 0.31.0.

It isn't limited to Flash. The call at `mla.py:235` runs on every sparse MLA layer, and on ROCm the only sparse backend is `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`, so no flag avoids it. #56604 notes the same crash on `GLM-5.2-FP8`, and the same call sits in `models/deepseek_v32/attention.py:496`, so DeepSeek-V3.2 on ROCm should fail too (we haven't run it). The GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 recipes both send AMD users to `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:latest`, which is v0.30.0 today.

Could #57252 go into a v0.30.1? If a patch release isn't planned, a known-issues line on the v0.30.0 release would save the next AMD user some time.

### Workaround

Adding the #57252 method to the installed file before `vllm serve` starts gets it running:

```python
def record_logical_topk_ready(self) -> None:
    pass
```

With that one change, the block starts in about 6.5 minutes, passes a known-answer prompt, a tool call and a 4 of 4 needle recall at 50K tokens, and served a 3 hour agentic load test through our gateway (8,272 requests, 0 errors).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Feature]: Add INT8 Support for KV Cache Quantization (Currently FP8-Only)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Hi vLLM team,

First, thanks for the amazing work on vLLM—it's been a game-changer for high-performance LLM serving! I'm writing to request a feature addition that would greatly benefit users with diverse hardware setups: support for INT8 quantization in KV Cache, alongside the existing FP8 implementation.

Current Behavior
As of vLLM version 0.4.0 (and confirmed in latest main branch), KV Cache quantization only supports FP8 (e.g., via quantization="fp8" in LLMEngine). While FP8 offers advantages for newer hardware (like NVIDIA H100), it lacks compatibility with older or mainstream GPUs (e.g., A100, RTX 4090, or cloud instances like AWS g5), which either don't support FP8 natively or incur significant overhead when emulating it.

Why INT8 Support is Needed
Hardware Accessibility:
FP8 requires SM9.0+ GPUs (H100+), but many production environments still use A100 (SM8.0) or consumer-grade cards. INT8 is universally supported across all modern NVIDIA GPUs (since Pascal architecture) and avoids FP8 emulation penalties.
Example: On an A100, forcing FP8 for KV Cache may degrade performance by 10–20% due to software emulation, while INT8 would run natively via Tensor Cores.
Memory Efficiency:
INT8 KV Cache reduces memory footprint by ~50% compared to FP16 (and similar to FP8), enabling larger batch sizes or longer context windows on memory-constrained devices. For instance:
FP16 KV Cache: 2 bytes/element
FP8/INT8 KV Cache: 1 byte/element
Unlike FP8, INT8 quantization is more mature and stable for asymmetric ranges (common in KV Cache activations), with proven results in frameworks like Hugging Face Transformers (quantize_kv_cache=True in model.generate()).
Use Case Demand:
Many users (myself included) deploy vLLM on cost-effective cloud instances (e.g., AWS p4d) where FP8 isn't viable. INT8 support would unlock wider adoption without sacrificing latency/throughput.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_
